Inherited from Ottoman Turkish هاله (hale), from Arabic هَالَة (hāla).
From Ottoman Turkish خلل (halel), from Arabic خَلَل (ḵalal).

From Ottoman Turkish خلخال (halhâl), from Arabic خَلْخَال (ḵalḵāl).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خالص (halis), from Arabic خَالِص (ḵāliṣ).

parole.significato: porter, carrier, a person who carries luggage and related objects for others
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish حمال (hamal, hammal), from Arabic حَمَّال (ḥammāl, “porter, carrier”).

From Ottoman Turkish حامی (hami), from Arabic حَامٍ (ḥāmin, “protector”).

parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish حامل, from Arabic حَامِل (ḥāmil).

parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish حامله (hamile), from Arabic حَامِلَة (ḥāmila), less common byform of حامِل (ḥāmil, “pregnant”, literally “carrying”).

From Ottoman Turkish حرف (harf), from Arabic حَرْف (ḥarf).

From Ottoman Turkish استناد (istinâd), from Arabic اِسْتِنَاد (istinād).

parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish استنساخ (istinsah, “hand-copying”), from Arabic اِسْتِنْسَاخ (istinsāḵ, “copying; cloning”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish استنطاق (istintâk), from Arabic اِسْتِنْطَاق (istinṭāq). Replaced by sorgu.
From Ottoman Turkish استراحت (istirahat), from Arabic اِسْتِرَاحَة (istirāḥa).

parole.significato: Istisqāʾ asking God for rain in times of drought
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish استسقا, from Arabic اِسْتِسْقَاء (istisqāʔ).

parole.significato: Taking advantage of or misusing someone's goodwill.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish استثمار (istismār) (which lacks written record), from Arabic اِسْتِثْمَار (istiṯmār, “investment”), verbal noun of اِسْتَثْمَرَ (istaṯmara, “to exploit, to invest”). Cognates with Azerbaijani istismar.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish استثنا, from Arabic اِسْتِثْنَاء (istiṯnāʔ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish استثنائی, from Arabic اِسْتِثْنَائِيّ (istiṯnāʔiyy). By surface analysis, istisna + -i.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish استوا (istivâ), from Arabic اِسْتِوَاء (istiwāʔ).
From Ottoman Turkish استیضاح (istizah), from Arabic اِسْتِيضَاح (istīḍāḥ).

parole.significato: istighfar, act of seeking forgiveness from God
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish استغفار (istiğfar), from Arabic اِسْتِغْفَار (istiḡfār).

parole.significato: An act of feigning reluctance towards an offer; playing coy, accismus.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish استغنا or استغناء (istiġnā, “a being sufficiently rich to have no need of help”), from Arabic اِسْتِغْنَاء (istiḡnāʔ), verbal noun of اِسْتَغْنَى (istaḡnā, “to be rich; to do without”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish استغراق (istiğrâk), from Arabic اِسْتِغْرَاق (istiḡrāq).
From Ottoman Turkish استشاره (istişare), from Arabic اِسْتِشَارَة (istišāra), verbal noun of اِسْتَشَارَ (istašāra).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish عصیان, from Arabic عِصْيَان (ʕiṣyān).
From Ottoman Turkish اطاعت (ita'at), from Arabic إِطَاعَة (ʔiṭāʕa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish عتاب, from Arabic عِتَاب (ʕitāb).
From Ottoman Turkish اطفائیه (itfâiyye), from Arabic إِطْفَائِيَّة (ʔiṭfāʔiyya).

parole.significato: An act of letting in, causing to enter.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ادخال (idḫal, itḫal, “a making or letting a person enter, introducing, inserting; an importing”), from Arabic إِدْخَال (ʔidḵāl, “introducing, causing to enter”), verbal noun of أَدْخَلَ (ʔadḵala, “to make enter, to let in, to introduce”).
From Ottoman Turkish ادخالات (idhalat), plural of ادخال (idhal), from Arabic إِدْخَال (ʔidḵāl). By surface analysis, ithal + -at.

parole.significato: The act of accusing; accusation, allegation.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اتهام (itham, “a suspecting (a person, of some offence), an imputing (an offence to a person), accusing someone of, holding someone guilty of something”), from Arabic اِتِّهَام (ittihām, “accusation, charge”), verbal noun of اِتَّهَمَ (ittahama, “to charge, to accuse”)
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اعتبار, borrowed from Arabic اِعْتِبَار (iʕtibār), from اِعْتَبَرَ (iʕtabara).
From Ottoman Turkish اعتباراً, from Arabic اِعْتِبَارًا (iʕtibāran), adverbial accusative of اِعْتِبَار (iʕtibār). By surface analysis, itibar (“consideration”) + -en.
From Ottoman Turkish اعتدال (i'tidal), from Arabic اِعْتِدَال (iʕtidāl).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اعتقاد (iʼtikâd), from Arabic اِعْتِقَاد (iʕtiqād).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اعتكاف (i’tikâf), from Arabic اِعْتِكَاف (iʕtikāf).
From Ottoman Turkish ایتلاف (itilâf), from Arabic اِئْتِلَاف (iʔtilāf).
From Ottoman Turkish اعتماد (itimad), from Arabic اِعْتِمَاد (iʕtimād).

parole.significato: Attention and care given to a task at hand; pains.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اعتنا (iʿtinā, “a giving serious attention, care, attention, importance”), from Arabic اِعْتِنَاء (iʕtināʔ), verbal noun of اِعْتَنَى (iʕtanā, “to look after, to take care, to nurse”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اعتراف, from Arabic اِعْتِرَاف (iʕtirāf).
From Ottoman Turkish اعتراض (i'tiraz), from Arabic اِعْتِرَاض (iʕtirāḍ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اعتیاد (iʿtiyād, “a repeatedly doing an act, a becoming habituated to; habit”), from Arabic اِعْتِيَاد (iʕtiyād)
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اعتذار (iʼtizâr), from Arabic اِعْتِذَار (iʕtiḏār).
From Ottoman Turkish اِتْلاف (itlâf), from Arabic إِتْلَاف (ʔitlāf).
From Ottoman Turkish اتمام (itmâm), from Arabic إِتْمَام (ʔitmām).

parole.significato: stipulation (something that is stated or stipulated as a condition of an agreement)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اتفاق (ittifâk) from Arabic اِتِّفَاق (ittifāq).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اتفاقا (ittifâken), from Arabic اِتِّفَاقًا (ittifāqan), adverbial accusative of اِتِّفَاق (ittifāq, “agreement”). By surface analysis, ittifak (“agreement”) + -en.
From Ottoman Turkish اتحاد (ittihad), from Arabic اِتِّحَاد (ittiḥād).
From Ottoman Turkish اتخاذ, from Arabic اِتِّخَاذ (ittiḵāḏ), verbal noun of اِتَّخَذَ (ittaḵaḏa, “to take, assume, adopt”).

parole.significato: An act of explaining; explanation, elucidation.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ایضاح (iżāḥ), from Arabic إِيضَاح (ʔīḍāḥ, “clarification”), verbal noun of أَوْضَحَ (ʔawḍaḥa, “to make clear, to clarify; to elucidate”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ازاله (izâle), from Arabic إِزَالَة (ʔizāla).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ازدواج (izdivac), from Arabic اِزْدِوَاج (izdiwāj).
From Ottoman Turkish اظهار (izhar), from Arabic إِظْهَار (ʔiẓhār).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اذن (izn, “permission”), borrowed from Arabic إِذْن (ʔiḏn, “permission”), from أَذِنَ (ʔaḏina).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اضمحلال (izmihlâl), from Arabic اِضْمِحْلَال (iḍmiḥlāl).
From Ottoman Turkish عزت (ʼizzet, “honor”), from Arabic عزة.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اجتهاد (ictihad), from Arabic اِجْتِهَاد (ijtihād).
From Ottoman Turkish اجتماع (ictima), from Arabic اِجْتِمَاع (ijtimāʕ).
From Ottoman Turkish اجتماعی (ictima'i), from Arabic اِجْتِمَاعِيّ (ijtimāʕiyy), equivalent to içtima (“assembly”) + -i (“nisba suffix”).
From Ottoman Turkish اجتماعیات (ictimaiyat), from Arabic اِجْتِمَاع (ijtimāʕ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اجتناب (ictinâb), from Arabic اِجْتِنَاب (ijtināb).
From Ottoman Turkish اشارت (işaret), from Arabic إِشَارَة (ʔišāra).

parole.significato: occupation (the control of a country or region by a hostile army)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish اشغال (işgal), Arabic إِشْغَال (ʔišḡāl).
From Ottoman Turkish عشرت (işret), from Arabic عِشْرَة (ʕišra).
From Ottoman Turkish اشتاه (iştah), from Arabic اِشْتِهاء (ištihāʔ).
From Ottoman Turkish اشتعال (iştial), from Arabic اِشْتِعَال (ištiʕāl), verbal noun of اِشْتَعَلَ (ištaʕala, “to ignite”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اشتغال (iştigal, “employment, occupation”), from Arabic اِشْتِغَال (ištiḡāl, “employment, occupation”).
From Ottoman Turkish اشتقاق (iştikak), from Arabic اِشْتِقَاق (ištiqāq).
From Ottoman Turkish اشترا (iştira), from Arabic اِشْتِرَاء (ištirāʔ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اشتراك (iştirak), borrowed from Arabic اِشْتِرَاك (ištirāk).
From Ottoman Turkish اشتیاق (iştiyak), from Arabic اِشْتِيَاق (ištiyāq).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اباضی (İbâżî), from Arabic إِبَاضِيّ (ʔibāḍiyy).
From Arabic إِلٰهِيّ (ʔilāhiyy, “my God”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish انجیل (incil), from Arabic إِنْجِيل (ʔinjīl), from Ancient Greek εὐαγγέλιον (euangélion, “good news”).

parole.significato: an owl; in particular the short-eared owl
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اسحاق (İshâk), borrowed from Arabic إِسْحَاق (ʔisḥāq), borrowed from Biblical Hebrew יִצְחָק (yiṣḥāq).
From Ottoman Turkish قباحت (kabahat), from Arabic قَبَاحَة (qabāḥa), verbal noun of قَبُحَ (qabuḥa, “to be vile, evil, infamous”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قابل (ḳābil, “that receives, accepts, or admits, who has capacity, intelligence, clever, skillful, possible, capable, susceptible”), from Arabic قَابِل (qābil), active participle of قَبِلَ (qabila, “to accept, to receive, to admit”).
From Ottoman Turkish قبیله (kabile), from Arabic قَبِيلَة (qabīla).
From Ottoman Turkish قابليت, from Arabic قَابِلِيَّة (qābiliyya).
From Ottoman Turkish قبر (kabr), from Arabic قَبْر (qabr).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قابض (“grasper, receiver, seizer; astringent, styptic”), from Arabic قَبْض (qabḍ, “to seize, to take hold of; to contract, to constrict; to constipate”).

parole.significato: Equal in amount or quantity; as much as.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قدر, from Old Anatolian Turkish قدر, from Arabic قَدْر (qadr).

parole.significato: Various kinds of pastry desserts such as kanafeh, typically drenched in hot syrup.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قطائف (ḳaṭaʿif, ḳaṭāyıf, “shaggy carpets, shaggy plushes with uncut loops, velvets, various kinds of sweet pastry and the material of which they are made”) (alternative form; قطایف (ḳadāyıf)), from Arabic قَطَايِف (qaṭāyif), the plural of قَطِيفَة (qaṭīfa). Doublet of kadife.
From Ottoman Turkish قدح (kadeh), from Arabic قَدَح (qadaḥ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قدم (kadem), from Arabic قَدَم (qadam).
From Ottoman Turkish قدمه (“step, stage, grade”), from Arabic قَدَمَة (qadama).
From Arabic قَدَر (qadar).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قطیفه (kadife, katife), from Arabic قَطِيفَة (qaṭīfa). Doublet of kadayıf.
From Ottoman Turkish قدیم (kadîm), from Arabic قَدِيم (qadīm).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قدر (kadr), from Arabic قَدْر (qadr).

From Ottoman Turkish قاضی, from Arabic قَاضٍ (qāḍin).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قفس (kafes), from Arabic قَفَص (qafaṣ).
From Ottoman Turkish قافله, from Arabic قَافِلَة (qāfila).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قافیه, from Arabic قَافِيَة (qāfiya).
From Ottoman Turkish قاهر (kâhir), from Arabic قَاهِر (qāhir).
From Ottoman Turkish قهقهه (kahkaha), from Arabic قَهْقَهَة (qahqaha).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قحبه (kahbe), derived from Arabic قَحْبَة (qaḥba, “whore”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قهوه (kahve), from Arabic قَهْوَة (qahwa). Doublet of kafe and kafeterya.

From Ottoman Turkish قهر (kahr), from Arabic قَهْر (qahr), verbal noun of قَهَرَ (qahara, “to oppress; to defeat”). The original sense was subjugation or calamity; the sense of the reaction to such an event evolved later.
From Ottoman Turkish قاعده (ka'ide, “rule”), from Arabic قَاعِدَة (qāʕida, “rule, principle”). See Azerbaijani qayda.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قائم (ḳaʾim, ḳayım, “that stands erect, perpendicular, rectangular, that exists permanently, especially God, the Existing One, that persists”), from Arabic قَائِم (qāʔim), active participle of قَامَ (qāma, “to stand up (to rise from lying or sitting position), to get u

parole.significato: cardamom, a perennial plant of the species Elettaria cardamomum, native to southern India
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قاقله (kakule), from Arabic قَاقُلَّة (qāqulla, “seepweed; various types of spices”), from Aramaic קָקוּלָא (qāqullā).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قالای (kalay), from Arabic قَلَعِيّ (qalaʕiyy, “tin”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قلباً (ḳalben), from Arabic قَلْبًا (qalban), adverbial accusative of قَلْب (qalb, “the heart”), equivalent to kalp (“heart”) + -en (Arabic adverbial suffix). Compare Azerbaijani qəlbən, Uzbek qalban, Uyghur قەلبەن (qelben).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قلبی (kalbî), from Arabic قَلْبِيّ (qalbiyy). By surface analysis, kalp (“heart”) + -î (nisba suffix).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قلندر (kalender), from Arabic قَلَنْدَر (qalandar), from Classical Persian کَلَنْدَر (kalandar).
From Ottoman Turkish قلفه (kalfa), from Arabic خَلِيفَة (ḵalīfa, literally “follower, successor”). Doublet of halife.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قلب (kalb, “heart”), from Arabic قَلْب (qalb).
From Ottoman Turkish قالپازان (kalpazan), from older قلبزن (kalbzen), from Arabic قَلْب (qalb, “reversal, transformation, perversion”) + Persian [Term?].

parole.significato: potash, the water-soluble part of the ash formed by burning plants
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قالیه (kalya), from Arabic قِلْي (qily, “potash; alkali”).
From Ottoman Turkish قالب (kalıp), from Arabic قَالِب (qālib).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قمر, from Arabic قَمَر (qamar).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قمری (kamerî), from Arabic قَمَرِيّ (qamariyy). By surface analysis, kamer (“moon”) + -î (nisba suffix).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قامت (kâmet), from Arabic قَامَة (qāma).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قاموس (kamus, “ocean; name of a celebrated Arabic dictionary”), from Arabic قَامُوسٌ (qāmūsun), from Ancient Greek ὠκεανός (ōkeanós). Doublet of okyanus.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قناعت (“contentment”), from Arabic قَنَاعَة (qanāʕa). The sense meaning opinion arose in early modern Turkish.
From Ottoman Turkish قانع (kani), from Arabic قَانِع (qāniʕ).

parole.significato: steelyard, or a scale in general
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قنطار (kantar), from Arabic قِنْطَار (qinṭār), from Byzantine Greek κεντηνάριον (kentēnárion), from Latin centēnārium.

parole.significato: law, statute, code, written set of rules
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قانون, from Arabic قَانُون (qānūn) (whence also Persian قانون), from Ancient Greek κανών (kanṓn). Cognate with English canon. Doublet of kanon.

parole.significato: By or according to law; legally.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قانیناً (ḳānunen), from Arabic قَانُونًا (qānūnan) adverbial accusative of قَانُون (qānūn, “law”). Equivalent to kanun (“law”) + -en (Arabic adverbial suffix).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قانونی (kanuni), from Arabic قَانُونِيّ (qānūniyy).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قاره (kara), from Arabic قَارَّة (qārra).
From Ottoman Turkish قرابت (karâbet), from Arabic قَرَابَة (qarāba).

parole.significato: carnation, any Eurasian flowering plant of the species Dianthus caryophyllus, widely cultivated for its flowers
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قرنفل (karanfil), from Arabic قَرَنْفُل (qaranful).
From Ottoman Turkish قرار, from Arabic قَرَار (qarār), verbal noun of قَرَّ (qarra).
From Ottoman Turkish قاری (kari), from Arabic قَارِئ (qāriʔ), active participle of قَرَأَ (qaraʔa, “to read”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قرینه (karine), from Arabic قَرِينَة (qarīna, “spouse; conjunction, linkage; evidence”).
From Ottoman Turkish قصبه, from Arabic قَصَبَة (qaṣaba).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قصاب (kasâb), from Arabic قَصَّاب (qaṣṣāb, “butcher”).
From Ottoman Turkish قساوت (kasâvet), from Arabic قَسَاوَة (qasāwa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قسم (kasem), from Arabic قَسَم (qasam).
From Ottoman Turkish قصیده, from Arabic قَصِيدَة (qaṣīda).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قصداً (kasdan, kasten), from Arabic قَصْدًا (qaṣdan).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قصدی, from Arabic قَصْد (qaṣd). By surface analysis, kasıt (“intent”) + -i (nisba suffix).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قاسم (kasım), from Arabic قَاسِم (qāsim).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قصد (kasd, “intent; intent to harm”), from Arabic قَصَدَ (qaṣada).

parole.significato: train, row, caravan, a group of animals, vehicles, or people that follow one another in a line
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قطار (“train, row, caravan; railway train”), from Arabic قِطَار (qiṭār, “row or line of camels; train”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قاتل (katil), from Arabic قَاتِل (qātil).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قتل (katl), from Arabic قَتْل (qatl).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قطعیاً (katʿiyyen), from Arabic قَطْعِيًّا (qaṭʕiyyan), adverbial accusative of قَطْعِيّ (qaṭʕiyy).
From Ottoman Turkish قطعیت, from Arabic قَطْعِيَّة (qaṭʕiyya). Cognate with Azerbaijani qətiyyət, Uzbek qatʼiyat and Uyghur قەتئىيەت (qet'iyet).

parole.significato: tar, a black, oily substance derived from organic materials such as wood, peat, or coal
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قطران (katran, “tar; asphalt”), from Arabic قَطْرَان (qaṭrān).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قطعی (katʿî), from Arabic قَطْعِيّ (qaṭʕiyy).

parole.significato: kaval, a traditional, oblique flute played throughout the Balkans and Anatolia
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قوال (kaval), probably from Arabic قَوَّال (qawwāl, “talkative; hymn singer”).
From Ottoman Turkish قواد (kavad, “guide; pander”), from Arabic قَوَّاد (qawwād).
From Ottoman Turkish قول (kavl), from Arabic قَوْل (qawl).

parole.significato: A group of people who share a common culture, language, traditions, as well as ancestry; a people, nation, tribe.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قوم (ḳavm, “a party, group, class of people, a people, nation”), from Old Anatolian Turkish قوم (qevm), from Arabic قَوْم (qawm, “people, nation, tribe”), from قَامَ (qāma, “to rise, to stand up”).

parole.significato: Limited portion of a curve, curvature.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قوس (kavis), from Arabic قوس (“bow, curve, twist”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قایمقام (kaymakam), from Arabic مَقَام قَائِم (qāʔim maqām, “stand in”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كدر (keder), from Arabic كَدَر (kadar), verbal noun of كَدِرَ (kadira, “to be muddy, to be turbid, to be gloomy”).

parole.significato: flax, a plant of the species Linum usitatissimum, cultivated as a food and fiber crop
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كتان (kettan, ketan), from Arabic كَتَّان (kattān, “flax; linen”), from Classical Syriac ܟܶܬܳܢܳܐ (kettānā, “flax; linen”).
Possibly from Ottoman Turkish قواده, feminine of قواد (kevad, “leader; pander”), that from Arabic قَوَّاد (qawwād) or Persian کواشه (kuwāša, “quality, way, manner”)
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كیفیت (keyfiyyet), from Arabic كَيْفِيَّة (kayfiyya). By surface analysis, keyif + -iyet. Cognate to Azerbaijani keyfiyyət.
From Ottoman Turkish كیفی (keyfi), from Arabic كَيْفِي (kayfī).

parole.significato: joy, pleasure, glee, delight, amusement, fun
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كیف (keyf), from Arabic كَيْف (kayf).
From Ottoman Turkish كذا (keza), from Arabic كَذَا (kaḏā)
From Ottoman Turkish كذلك, from Arabic كَذَلِك (kaḏalik)
From Ottoman Turkish كشف (keşf), from Arabic كَشْف (kašf), verbal noun of كَشَفَ (kašafa, “to remove, uncover, reveal, expose, investigate”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كبار (kibâr), from Arabic كِبَار (kibār).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كبر (kibr), from Arabic كِبْر (kibr).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كفایت (kifāyet), from Arabic كِفَايَة (kifāya).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كلس, from Arabic كِلْس (lime).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كیمیا (kimiya, kimya), from Arabic كِيمِيَاء (kīmiyāʔ), from Ancient Greek χυμείᾱ (khumeíā).

parole.significato: cumin, a flowering plant of the species Cuminum cyminum and its aromatic seed
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كمیون (kimyon), from Arabic كَمُّون (kammūn), from Aramaic כַּמֹּונָֹא / ܩܰܡܽܘܢܳܐ (kammōnā, “cumin”), from Akkadian 𒌑𒁷𒊺𒉪 (Ú.GAMUN /⁠kamūnu⁠/, “cumin”), from Sumerian [Term?] (/⁠gamun⁠/, “cumin”).

parole.significato: An expression that conveys the thought indirectly; an allusion, innuendo.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كنایه (kinaye), from Arabic كِنَايَة (kināya).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كرا, from Arabic كِرَاء (kirāʔ, “rent, renting”).

parole.significato: kisbet, a form of lederhosen, traditionally made from the hide of water buffalo and often made from calfskin in modern…
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كسبت (kispet), from earlier كسوت, from Arabic كِسْوَة (kiswa). Doublet of kisve and kisvet.
From Ottoman Turkish كسوت, from Arabic كِسْوَة (kiswa). Doublet of kisbet and kispet.
From Arabic كِتَابَة (kitāba).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كتابت (kitâbet), from Arabic كِتَابَة (kitāba).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كتاب, borrowed from Arabic كِتَاب (kitāb).

parole.significato: mass (quantity of matter cohering together to make one body)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كتله, from Arabic كُتْلَة (kutla, “mass, cluster”). Doublet of kütle.

parole.significato: tragacanth, a gum extracted from several species of plants in the genus Astragalus
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كتره (kitre), vulgar form of earlier كثیرا (kesira), from Arabic كَثِيرَاء (kaṯīrāʔ, “tragacanth”).

From kon- (“to be put down”) + -u (deverbal nominal suffix), a calque of Arabic مَوْضُوع (mawḍūʕ, “that which is laid down”), itself a calque of Ancient Greek ὑποκείμενον (hupokeímenon, “that which is laid down”). Coined in 1933 from a suggestion by a member of the public in the newspaper Hakimiyet-

From Ottoman Turkish قرصان (korsan, “pirate”), from Arabic قُرْصَان (qurṣān, “pirate”), from Italian corsale (“corsair, privateer”), from Medieval Latin cursārius (“pirate, sea-raider”), from Latin cursus (“course, a running; plunder, hostile inroad”). Doublet of kurs and kur.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قبه (kubbe), from Arabic قُبَّة (qubba).

parole.significato: power, might, strength, puissance, the ability to do or undergo something
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قدرت (kudret, “power, might”), from Arabic قُدْرَة (qudra, “power, capacity”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قله (kulle), borrowed from Arabic قُلَّة (qulla, “peak, summit, top”).

parole.significato: severe pain felt throughout the body, especially in the shoulders
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قولنج (kulunc, “colic; cramp”), from Arabic قَوْلَنْج (qawlanj, “colic, colitis”), ultimately from Ancient Greek κωλικός (kōlikós, “suffering in the colon”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قمار (kumar), from Arabic قِمَار (qimār).
From Arabic قُمَاش (qumāš).
From Ottoman Turkish قمری (kumru), from Old Anatolian Turkish, from Arabic قُمْرِيّ (qumriyy, “laughing dove”). Cognate with Turkmen gumry (“laughing dove”), etc.

parole.significato: Choosing the outcome among two or more candidates by chance; drawing lots, drawing straws.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قرعه, from Arabic قُرْعة (qurʕa).

From Ottoman Turkish قرابیه (kurabiye), غرابیه (gurabiye, “an almond-biscuit; a small hunting-case watch”), a pseudo-Arabism like جمهوریت (cumhuriyet) suffixed ـیت (-iyyet) from Arabic غُرَاب (ḡurāb, “the extremity of the haunch, bend of the scabbard”) because the fob watch was carried near the haun
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قربان (kurban), borrowed from Arabic قُرْبَان (qurbān), borrowed from Aramaic קורבנא (qurbānā).
From Arabic كُسْكُس (kuskus), from a Berber language.
From Ottoman Turkish قصور (kusur), from Arabic قُصُور (quṣūr). First attested in the 18th century.

Phono-semantic matching of Arabic قُدْس (quds)/قدسي (qudsiyy), by surface analysis, kut (“luck, good fortune”) + -sal. Alternatively, from kutsa (“to bless”) + -(I)l. Compare tükel (“complete, perfect”) for derivation.
From Ottoman Turkish قطب (kutb, vulg. kutub, kutup), from Arabic قُطْب (quṭb).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قوت (kuvvet), from Arabic قُوَّة (quwwa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كابوس, borrowed from Arabic كَابُوس (kābūs), borrowed from Classical Syriac ܟܒܘܫܐ (kāḇōšā, “nightmare, incubus”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كافی (kāfi, “sufficing, sufficient, The All-Sufficing God”), from Arabic كَافٍ (kāfin), active participle of كَفَى (kafā, “to be enough for (someone), to protect, to spare”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كافر (kâfir), from Arabic كَافِر (kāfir, “unbeliever”).

parole.significato: camphor, a waxy, colorless solid with a strong aroma extracted from the wood of the camphor tree
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كافور (kâfur, “camphor”), borrowed from Arabic كَافُور (kāfūr, “camphor”), possibly borrowed from Middle Persian 𐭪𐭠𐭯𐭥𐭫 (kʾpʿl /⁠kāpūr⁠/), borrowed from an Austronesian language, from Proto-Austronesian *qapuʀ.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كاهل (kâhil), from Arabic كَاهِل (kāhil).

parole.significato: clairvoyant, seer, soothsayer (one who foretells the future)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish كاهن (ḱahin), from Arabic كَاهِن (kāhin).
From Ottoman Turkish كائن, from Arabic كَائِن (kāʔin).
From Ottoman Turkish كائنات (ḱa'inat), from Arabic كَائِنَات (kāʔināt).

parole.significato: complete, perfect, morally or spiritually mature
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كامل (kâmil), from Arabic كَامِل (kāmil).

parole.significato: The first two months of winter
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كانون (kânûn, “hearth; first two months of winter”), from Arabic كَانُون (kānūn, “hearth”), from Aramaic כָּנוֹנָא / ܟܢܘܢܐ (kānōnā, “brazier”), from Akkadian 𒆠𒉈 (KI.NE /⁠kanūnu⁠/, “brazier, kiln, stove, hearth; a name of a ritual and also the month it takes place”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كانون اول (kanun-ı evvel), from Arabic كَانُون الأَوَّل (kānūn al-ʔawwal), from Classical Syriac ܟܢܘܢ ܐ. By surface analysis, kânun + evvel (“first”). The name was officially changed to Aralık by law number 4696 passed January 10, 1945.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كانون ثانی (kanun-ı sani), from Arabic كَانُونُ الثَّانِي (kānūnu ṯ-ṯānī), from Classical Syriac ܟܢܘܢ ܒ. By surface analysis, kânun + sani (“second”). The name was officially changed to Ocak by law number 4696 passed January 10, 1945.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كاتب (ḱatib), from Arabic كَاتِب (kātib, “clerk”).

parole.significato: A person who discovers something that previously existed; a discoverer, an explorer.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كاشف (kāşif, “who discovers or reveals, who investigates, who estimates the value, (formerly) a kind of sheriff under the Memluks in Egypt”), from Arabic كَاشِف (kāšif, “reagent, radio detector”), active participle of كَشَفَ (kašafa, “to uncover, to reveal, to expose,

parole.significato: a military class made of slaves
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كولهمن (kölemen). Equivalent to köle (“slave”) + -men (noun-forming suffix). Nişanyan suggests a borrowing from Arabic غِلْمَان (ḡilmān, “slaves”), phonetically influenced by köle.

parole.significato: a deep basket made of wood or reeds
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish كفه (küfe), from Arabic كُفَّة (kuffa).
From Ottoman Turkish كفر (küfür), from Arabic كُفْر (kufr), with semantic shift.
From Ottoman Turkish كل (kül), from Arabic كُلّ (kull).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كلفت (külfet), borrowed from Arabic كُلْفَة (kulfa).

parole.significato: complete works of an author, corpus
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish كلیات (külliyat, “universal; complete works”), from Arabic كُلِّيَّات (kulliyyāt), plural of كُلِّيَّة (kulliyya).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كلیه (külliye), from Arabic كُلِّيَّة (kulliyya).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كلیاً (külliyen), from Arabic كُلِّيًّا (kulliyyan), adverbial accusative of كُلِّيّ (kulliyy), from كُلّ (kull, “each, every, whole, all”) + ـِيّ (-iyy, nisba suffix).
From Ottoman Turkish كومه (küme), from Arabic كَوْمَة (kawma).

parole.significato: kanafeh; a kind of dessert with an Arabic origin, made of cheese and served hot.
parole.testo: From Arabic كُنافة (kunāfa), possibly from Coptic ⲕⲉⲛⲉⲫⲓⲧⲉⲛ (kenephiten).

parole.significato: The record that shows a person's identity information; kunya.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كنیه (kinye, künye), from Arabic كُنْيَة (kunya).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كره (küre), from Arabic كُرَة (kura, “ball”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كرسی (kürsi), from Arabic كُرْسِيّ (kursiyy), from Classical Syriac ܟܘܪܣܝܐ (kursəyā), from Akkadian 𒄑𒄖𒍝 (kussûm), from Sumerian 𒄑𒄖𒍝 (^(g̃eš)gu-za /⁠guza⁠/, “chair”).
From Ottoman Turkish كسور (küsûr), from Arabic كُسُور (kusūr).

parole.significato: mass (quantity of matter cohering together to make one body)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish كتله (kütle), from Arabic كُتْلَة (kutla). Doublet of kitle.
From Ottoman Turkish كئول (küul), from Arabic كُئُول (kuʔūl).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كوشنه (küşne, “kind of vetch”), from Arabic كُشْنَى (kušnā, “Vicia palaestina”), ultimately from Classical Syriac ܟܘܫܢܐ (kūšnā).

parole.significato: qibla; the direction in which Muslims face while praying, now the Kaaba in Mecca.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قبله (kıble), from Arabic قِبْلَة (qibla).
From Ottoman Turkish قدم (kıdem), from Arabic قِدَم (qidam).
From Ottoman Turkish قلاده (kılâde), from Arabic قِلَادَة (qilāda).
From Ottoman Turkish قلف (kılıf), from Arabic غِلَاف (ḡilāf).
Possibly an alteration of Ottoman Turkish قمل (kaml, “lice”), from Arabic قَمْل (qaml, “lice”).

parole.significato: henna, a reddish dye used for temporary tattoos and hair coloring
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قنا (kına), from Arabic حِنَّاء (henna).
From Ottoman Turkish قبطی, from Arabic قِبْطِيّ (qibṭiyy).

parole.significato: An act of reading or reciting.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قرائت (ḳırāʾat, “a reading; a reading or reciting the Qur'an in a solemn or artistic manner, (pl. "قرآات") a special method of pronouncing each word of the Qur'an”), from Arabic قِرَاءَة (qirāʔa, “reading”), verbal noun of قَرَأَ (qaraʔa, “to read, to recite”).

parole.significato: waterskin, a container for water made of tanned skin
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قربه (kırba), itself from Arabic قِرْبَة (qirba, “waterskin”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قرمز (kırmız), Arabic قِرْمِز (qirmiz).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قرمزی, from Arabic قِرْمِزِيّ (qirmiziyy) or Persian قِرمِز (qermez), from Persian کِرمِست (kêrmêst) ultimately from Proto-Indo-Iranian *kŕ̥miš (“worm”). By surface analysis, kırmız (“kermes”) + -i (“nisbah suffix”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قرطاسيه (kırtasiye), from Arabic قرطاس (qirṭās, “paper”) + -iye (“suffix indicating a place”), ultimately from Ancient Greek χάρτης (khártēs, “papyrus, paper”).

parole.significato: Punishing the guilty in the same way they committed the crime; talion.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قصاص (ḳıṣaṣ, ḳaṣaṣ, “the application of the law of talion, putting a man to death for manslaughter”), from Arabic قِصَاص (qiṣāṣ), verbal noun of قَاصَّ (qāṣṣa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قسماً (kısmen), from Arabic قِسْمًا (qisman), adverbial accusative of قِسْم (qism).
From Ottoman Turkish قسمت (kısmet), from Arabic قِسْمَة (qisma).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قصه (kıssa), from Arabic قِصَّة (qiṣṣa).
From Arabic قِسْطَاس (qisṭās).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قسم (kısm, kısım), from Arabic قِسْم (qism).

A recent adaptation in the southeast of Arabic كِسَر (kisar, “fragments”), less likely an alternative vocalization of كَسْر (kasr, “fraction, breaking”) or even كِسْر (kisr, “limb”) when used after a name of a cooking-pot meaning a pot “of several things joined together”.
From Ottoman Turkish قطعه (kıt'a), from Arabic قِطْعَة (qiṭʕa).
From Ottoman Turkish قطعات (kıtaat), plural of قطعه (kıta), from Arabic قِطْعَة (qiṭʕa). Formally, the Arabic plural of kıta.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قوام (kıvâm), from Arabic قِوَام (qiwām).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قیافت, from Arabic قِيَافَة (qiyāfa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قیامت (kıyâmet), from Arabic قِيَامَة (qiyāma, “resurrection, upheaval”), from قَامَ (qāma, “to stand up (to rise from lying or sitting position), to get up”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قیاس (kıyâs), from Arabic قِيَاس (qiyās).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قیاسی (kıyâsî), from Arabic قِيَاسِيّ (qiyāsiyy). By surface analysis, kıyas + -i.
From Ottoman Turkish قیمت (kıymet, kımet), from Arabic قِيمَة (qīma).

parole.significato: There is no deity but God (the shahada)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لا اله الا الله, Arabic لا إله إلا الله (lā ʔilāha ʔillā llāhu).
From Ottoman Turkish لااقل (laakal), from Arabic عَلَى اَلْأَقَلّ (ʕalā l-ʔaqall).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لادن, from Arabic لَادَن (lādan, “gum cistus”), from Ancient Greek λᾱ́δᾰνον (lā́dănon).
From Ottoman Turkish لاادری (lâedri), from Arabic لَاأَدْرِيّ (lāʔadriyy).
From Ottoman Turkish لفظ (lafz), from Arabic لَفْظ (lafẓ).
From Ottoman Turkish لاحقه (lahıka), from Arabic لَاحِقَة (lāḥiqa).

parole.significato: tomb with brick or stone walls; a sarcophagus
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لحد (laḥd), from Arabic لَحْد (laḥd).
From Arabic لَحْم عَجِين (laḥm ʕajīn, literally “meat and dough”), from لَحْم (laḥm, “meat”) + عَجِين (ʕajīn, “dough”).
From Ottoman Turkish لحظه, from Arabic لَحْظَة (laḥẓa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لعین (laʼin, “cursed, damned”), from Arabic لَعِين (laʕīn, “cursed, execrable”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لقب (laḳab), from Arabic لَقَب (laqab).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لاقید (lā ḳayd, “"There is no need for anxiety;" who feels no care or anxiety”), from Arabic لَا قَيْد (lā qayd), from لَا (lā, “no, not”) and قَيْد (qayd, “chain, bond, restriction, registration”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لكن (lâkin), borrowed from Arabic لٰكِن (lākin).

parole.significato: Letter of the Arabic alphabet: ل
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لام (lâm), from Arabic لَام (lām).
From Arabic لَام (lām) + أَلِف (ʔalif).

parole.significato: curse, malediction, a prayer or imprecation that harm may befall someone
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لعنت (laʼnet, “curse, malediction”), from Arabic لَعْنَة (laʕna, “curse, anathema”).
From Ottoman Turkish لطیف (latîf), from Arabic لَطِيف (laṭīf).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لطیفه (latife), from Arabic لَطِيفَة (laṭīfa).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لاابالی (la-ubāli, “(I care not), careless, free and easy”), from Arabic لَا أُبَالِي (lā ʔubālī, “I don't care”), from لَا (lā, “no, not”) and أُبَالِي (ʔubālī), non-past (imperfect) indicative of بَالَى (bālā, “to care about, to notice, to pay attention”).
From Ottoman Turkish لایموت (layemut), from Arabic لَا يَمُوتُ (lā yamūtu).
From Ottoman Turkish لایحه (layiha), from Arabic لَائِحَة (lāʔiḥa). Compare Azerbaijani layihə.
From Ottoman Turkish لایق, from Arabic لَائِق (lāʔiq).
From Ottoman Turkish لازم (lâzım), ultimately from Arabic لَازِم (lāzim).
From Ottoman Turkish لغو (lağv), from Arabic لَغْو (laḡw). Compare Azerbaijani ləğv.
From Ottoman Turkish لبلبی (leblebi, “roasted chickpea; jumbled or mashed chickpea”), from Arabic لَبْلَابِيّ (lablābiyy, “chickpea stew”).

parole.significato: Being in favor of, favorable for or to a thing or person; one's benefit.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish له (leh, “for him/it; in favor of him/it; to, belonging to him/it”), from Arabic لَهُ (lahu).
From Ottoman Turkish لهیم, borrowed from Arabic لَحْم (laḥm).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لهجه (lehce), from Arabic لَهْجَة (lahja).
From Ottoman Turkish لطافت (letafet), from Arabic لَطَافَة (laṭāfa).
From Ottoman Turkish لوازم (levazım), from Arabic لَوَازِم (lawāzim), plural of لَازِم (lāzim, “necessary”).

parole.significato: inscription hung on a wall, signboard
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish لوحه (levha), itself from Arabic لَوْحَة (lawḥa, “plank, board, blackboard”).

parole.significato: lilac, any large, flowering shrub of the genus Syringa, especially Syringa vulgaris
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لیلاق (leylak), from Arabic لَيْلَك (laylak, “lilac”), itself from Classical Persian لِیلَک (līlak, “indigo; lilac”).

parole.significato: stork, any large wading bird with long legs and a long beak of the family Ciconiidae
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لیلك (leylek), colloquial variant of لكلك (leklek, leylek, “stork”), from Arabic لَقْلَق (laqlaq, “stork”).
From Ottoman Turkish لیلی (leyli, “nocturnal”), from Arabic لَيْلِيّ (layliyy), from لَيْل (layl, “night”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لذیذ (lezîz), from Arabic لَذِيذ (laḏīḏ).
From Ottoman Turkish لذت (lezzet, “taste; plesant taste”), from Arabic لَذَّة (laḏḏa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لسان (lisân, “tongue, language”), from Old Anatolian Turkish لِسٰانۡ (lisān), from Arabic لِسَان (lisān, “tongue”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لسانی (lisânî), from Arabic لِسَانِيّ (lisāniyy). By surface analysis, lisan (“language”) + -i (nisba suffix).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لواطه (livâta, livâte), لواطت (livâtet, livâtat), from Old Anatolian Turkish لواطت (livātat), from Arabic لِوَاطَة (liwāṭa).
From Ottoman Turkish لیاقت (liyakat, “merit”), from Arabic لِيَاقَة (liyāqa).

parole.significato: kind of short and thick stick used as a weapon by soldiers during sieges, or as a training tool for cavalrymen to impro…
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لوبوط (lobut, “short and thick stick”), from a vulgarized form of Arabic نَبُوت (nabūt, “thick branch or stick”).
From Ottoman Turkish لوقوم (lokum), لقوم (lokum), from Arabic رَاحَة الْحُلْقُوم (rāḥa(t) al-ḥulqūm, “throat comfort”).
From Ottoman Turkish لغت (lüğat), from Arabic لُغَة (luḡa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لطفاً (lutfen, “as a favor, as a kindness”), from Arabic لُطْفًا (luṭfan), adverbial accusative of لُطْف (luṭf, “kindness, friendliness”).
From Ottoman Turkish لطف (lütf), Arabic لُطْف (luṭf).
From Ottoman Turkish لزوم (lüzum), from Arabic لُزُوم (luzūm).
From Ottoman Turkish معالاسف (ma'alesef), from Arabic مَعَ الْأَسَف (maʕa al-ʔasaf, literally “with regret”); compare Persian معالاسف (ma'-al-asaf, “unfortunately”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مع الممنونیه (ma’a l-memnuniye), from Arabic مَعَ الْمَمْنُونِيَّة (maʕa al-mamnūniyya).
From Ottoman Turkish مع ما فیه (maamafih), from Arabic مَعَ مَا فِيهِ (maʕa mā fīhi).
From Ottoman Turkish معارف, from Arabic مَعَارِف (maʕārif), plural of مَعْرِفَة (maʕrifa, “knowledge, learning”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish معاش, borrowed from Arabic مَعَاش (maʕāš), from عَاشَ (ʕāša).
From Ottoman Turkish مابعد (mabad), from Arabic مَا بَعْد (mā baʕd).
From Ottoman Turkish معبد (ma'bed), from Arabic مَعْبَد (maʕbad). Cognate of Azerbaijani məbəd.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish معبود (ma'bûd), from Arabic مَعْبُود (maʕbūd).

parole.significato: paste, any soft and moist mixture of several ingredients incorporated together
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish معجون (maʼcun, “paste; putty”), itself from Arabic مَعْجُون (maʕjūn, “paste; putty”).
From Ottoman Turkish ماده (madde), from Arabic مَادَّة (mādda).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مادی (maddi), from Arabic مَادِّيّ (māddiyy). By surface analysis, madde (“material”) + -i (nisba suffix).
From Arabic مَا دَامَ (mā dāma).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish معدن (maden), borrowed from Arabic مَعْدِن (maʕdin), from عَدَنَ (ʕadana).
From Ottoman Turkish معدنی, from Arabic مَعْدِنِيّ (maʕdiniyy). By surface analysis, maden (“mineral”) + -i (nisba suffix).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مفصل (mafsal), from Arabic مَفْصِل (mafṣil, “knuckle; joint”).
From Ottoman Turkish محل (mahal), from Arabic مَحَلّ (maḥall).

parole.significato: neighbourhood, quarter (division or section of a town or city)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish محله (“station; parish, ward”), from Arabic مَحَلَّة (maḥalla).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محلی, from Arabic مَحَلِّيّ (maḥalliyy).
From Ottoman Turkish مهارت, from Arabic مَهَارَة (mahāra).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محبوبه (mahbube), from Arabic مَحْبُوبَة (maḥbūba). Compare Azerbaijani məhbubə.
From Ottoman Turkish محبوب (mahbûb), from Arabic مَحْبُوب (maḥbūb).
From Ottoman Turkish محجوب (mahcûb, “curtained, veiled, secluded, ashamed, bashful”), from Arabic مَحْجُوب (maḥjūb).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مخدوم (mahdum), from Arabic مَخْدُوم (maḵdūm).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محدود (mahdud), from Arabic مَحْدُود (maḥdūd).

parole.significato: howdah, mihaffa, a covered litter positioned on the back of a camel or elephant, usually to carry female passengers
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محفه (mahfe), from Arabic مِحَفَّة (miḥaffa, “covered howdah”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مخفی (mahfî), from Arabic مَخْفِيّ (maḵfiyy).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محفوظ (mahfûz), from Arabic مَحْفُوظ (maḥfūẓ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ماهر (mhhir), from Arabic مَاهِر (māhir).
From Ottoman Turkish ماهیت, from Arabic مَاهِيَّة (māhiyya).

parole.significato: A court of law, court of justice, tribunal.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محكمه (maḥkeme, “a court of justice, tribunal, especially of the cannon law of Islam”), from Arabic مَحْكَمَة (maḥkama, “court”), verbal noun of حَكَمَ (ḥakama, “to exercise authority, to command, to bid, to rule”).

parole.significato: the losing party of a case
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محكوم علیه (mahkûmün aleyh), from Arabic مَحْكُومٌ عَلَيْه (maḥkūmun ʕalayh). By surface analysis, mahkum + aleyh.

parole.significato: the winning party of a case
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محكوم له (mahkûmün leh), from Arabic مَحْكُومٌ لَه (maḥkūmun lah). By surface analysis, mahkum + leh.
From Ottoman Turkish محكوم (mahḱum), from Arabic مَحْكُوم (maḥkūm). See Azerbaijani məhkum.
From Ottoman Turkish مخلص (mahlas), from Arabic مَخْلَص (maḵlaṣ).

parole.significato: mahleb, a Middle Eastern spice derived from the pit of the mahaleb cherry
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محلب (mahleb), from Arabic مَحْلَب (maḥlab, “mahaleb cherry”).

parole.significato: A creature, any created thing, especially living.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مخلوق (maḫluḳ, “created, a creature”), from Arabic مَخْلُوق (maḵlūq, “creature”), passive participle of خَلَقَ (ḵalaqa, “to create, to make, to shape”).

parole.significato: mahmal, a ceremonial litter without a passenger that was carried by pilgrims on the hajj
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محمل (mahmil, mahmel), from Arabic مَحْمَل (maḥmal, “camel litter, howdah”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مخمور (mahmûr), from Arabic مَخْمُور (maḵmūr).

parole.significato: spur, a rigid implement fixed to one's heel for the purpose of prodding a horse
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مهموز (mahmuz), itself from Arabic مِهْمَاز (mihmāz, “prod, spur, goad”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محبوس (mahbus, “imprisoned, a prisoner, given in mortmain for the service of God”), from Arabic مَحْبُوس (maḥbūs), passive participle of حَبَسَ (ḥabasa, “to imprison, to hold back”).
From Ottoman Turkish محرمه, from Arabic مَحْرَمَة (maḥrama).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محرم (mahrem), from Arabic مَحْرَم (maḥram).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محروم (mahrum), from Arabic مَحْرُوم (maḥrūm).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محروقات (mahrûkat, “fuel”), from Arabic مَحْرُوقَات (maḥrūqāt).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محصول (mahsul), borrowed from Arabic مَحْصُول (maḥṣūl).
From Ottoman Turkish محصور (mahsur), from Arabic مَحْصُور (maḥṣūr), passive participle of حَصَرَ (ḥaṣara).

parole.significato: [with dative] peculiar to, specific to, particular to
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish مخصوص (mahsus), from Arabic مَخْصُوص (maḵṣūṣ, “private, special, characteristic”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ﻣﺤﺴﻮﺱ (mahsus), from Arabic مَحْسُوس (maḥsūs, “felt, perceptible”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مخوف, from Arabic مَخُوف (maḵūf), passive participle of خَافَ (ḵāfa).

parole.significato: Mahya lights (decorative lights strung up between the minarets of Turkish mosques to form illuminated words or pictures…
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ماهیه (mahiyye, “monthly (pay or allowance)”), pseudo-Arabism from Persian ماه (māh / mâh, “month”) + Arabic ـِيَّة (-iyya).

parole.significato: cellar; an enclosed underground space, often under a building; used for storage or shelter
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مخزن (mahzen), from Arabic مَخْزَن (maḵzan). Doublet of mağaza and magazin.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محزون (maḥzun, “saddened, grieved, sorry, melancholy”), from Arabic مَحْزُون (maḥzūn), passive participle of حَزَنَ (ḥazana, “to make sad, to sadden”).

parole.significato: destruction, annihilation, ruin, downfall or being destroyed, annihilated
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish محو (mahv, “a causing not to exist, an annihilating”), from Arabic مَحْو (maḥw) verbal noun of مَحَا (maḥā, “to erase, to destroy”).

parole.significato: The place where humanity will assemble on the day of judgement, often identified with Mount Arafat in near Mecca.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish محشر (mahşer, “gathering place; crowd; assembly on judgment day”), from Arabic مَحْشَر (maḥšar, “place of assembly”), from حَشَرَ (ḥašara, “assemble”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish معیشت (maişet), from Arabic مَعِيشَة (maʕīša).
From Ottoman Turkish مقاله (makale), from Arabic مَقَالَة (maqāla).

parole.significato: Melodic mode. The makam system sets complex rules for cins (characteristic intervals) and seyir (melodic development) i…
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مقام (makam), from Arabic مَقَام (maqām).

parole.significato: seat; center of power, headquarters, capital
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish مقر (makar), from Arabic مَقَرّ (maqarr).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مقره (makara, “pulley, block”), from Arabic بَكَرَة (bakara, “pulley, block”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مقص (makas), from Arabic مِقَصّ (miqaṣṣ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مقعد (makʼad), from Arabic مَقْعَد (maqʕad).
From Arabic مَقْبُول (maqbūl), passive participle of قَبِلَ (qabila).

parole.significato: receipt (written acknowledgment that a specified article or sum of money has been received)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مقبوض (maqbuz, “grasped, received, seized, laid hold of”), from Arabic مقبوض (maḳbūḍ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مقرمه, from Arabic مِقْرَمَة (miqrama, “ornamental fringe, embroidered veil”), from مِقْرَم (miqram, “bedspread”).
From Ottoman Turkish مقصد (maksad, maksıd), from Arabic مَقْصَد (maqṣad).

parole.significato: the last line of a qasida or ghazal
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish مقطع, from Arabic مَقْطَع (maqṭaʕ).
From Ottoman Turkish مقطوع (maktû'), from Arabic مَقْطُوع (maqṭūʕ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مقطوعا (maktuan), derived from Arabic مَقْطُوعًا (maqṭūʕan), adverbial accusative of مَقْطُوع (maqṭūʕ). By surface analysis, maktu + an (adverbial suffix).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مقتول (maktul), from Arabic مَقْتُول (maqtūl).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish معقول (ma'kûl), from Arabic مَعْقُول (maʕqūl).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish معكوس, from Arabic مَعْكُوس (maʕkūs).
From Ottoman Turkish مال (mal), from Arabic مَال (māl, “property”).
From Ottoman Turkish مالی (mali), from Arabic مَالِيّ (māliyy). By surface analysis, mal + -i.
From Ottoman Turkish مالیه (maliye), from Arabic مَالِيَّة (māliyya), feminine of مَالِيّ (māliyy), nisba of مَال (māl). Compare Azerbaijani maliyyə.
From Ottoman Turkish مالیت (mâliyet), from Arabic مَالِيَّة (māliyya).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish معلول (māʿlul), from Arabic مَعْلُول (maʕlūl).

parole.significato: In an injured or sick state.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish معلولاً (mʿālulen), from Arabic مَعْلُولًا (maʕlūlan) adverbial accusative of مَعْلُول (maʕlūl).
From Ottoman Turkish معلوم (ma'lum), from Arabic مَعْلُوم (maʕlūm).
From Ottoman Turkish معلومات (maʼlumat), from Arabic مَعْلُومَات (maʕlūmāt). The singular form مَعْلُوم (maʕlūm) yielded malum (“known”).
From Arabic مِلْزَمَة (milzama), if not مَا لَازِم (mā lāzim).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish معنا, from Arabic مَعْنًى (maʕnan) (plural: مَعَانٍ (maʕānin)).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish منجنیق (mancanık, mancınık), from Arabic مَنْجَنِيق (manjanīq), ultimately from Ancient Greek μαγγανικά (manganiká).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish معنوي (manevi), from Arabic مَعْنَوِيّ (maʕnawiyy).
From Ottoman Turkish معنویات (maneviyat), plural of Arabic مَعْنَوِيّ (maʕnawiyy).

parole.significato: An open-top fireplace, made of sheet metal, copper or brass, used for either heat or cooking; a brasier or a barbecue.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مانغال (mangal) or منقل (manḳal, “a brasier, chafing dish for charcoal fire”),) from Arabic مَنْقُول (manqūl, “portable, movable”). Cognate with Armenian մանղալ (manġal), Azerbaijani manqal, Bulgarian мангал (mangal), Greek μανγκάλ (mangkál) Macedonian мангал (mangal),
From Ottoman Turkish مانی (mani), from Arabic مَعْنًى (maʕnan).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish منطق, from Arabic مَنْطِق (manṭiq, “speech”). Cognate with Azerbaijani məntiq, Uzbek mantiq.

parole.significato: According to, as per logic; logically.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish منطقاً (mantıken), from Arabic مَنْطِقًا (manṭiqan) adverbial accusative of مَنْطِق (manṭiq).
From Ottoman Turkish منطقی, from Arabic مَنْطِقِيّ (manṭiqiyy).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish منظره, from Arabic مَنْظَرَة (manẓara).
From Ottoman Turkish منظوم (manzum), from Arabic مَنْظُوم (manẓūm).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish منظومه (manzume), from Arabic مَنْظُومَة (manẓūma).

parole.significato: A sharecropper; a landless agricultural laborer who works on a landowner's field in exchange for a share of the crops.
parole.testo: From Arabic مُرَابَعَة (murābaʕa).
From Ottoman Turkish مرض (maraz), from Arabic مَرَض (maraḍ).
From Ottoman Turkish معرفت (maʼrifet, maʼrıfet), from Arabic مَعْرِفَة (maʕrifa).

parole.significato: gammon, a victory in backgammon achieved when the opponent has not borne off a single stone
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مارس (mars, “gammon”); further etymology is unclear. According to Nishanyan, it could derive from Arabic مَرِس (maris, “of practice, experienced”).
From Ottoman Turkish معروف (maruf), from Arabic مَعْرُوف (maʕrūf).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مارونی (Mârûnî), from Arabic مَارُونِيّ (mārūniyy). By surface analysis, Marun + -i (nisba suffix).
From Ottoman Turkish معروض (“maruz”), from Arabic مَعْرُوض (maʕrūḍ), passive participle of عَرَضَ (ʕaraḍa, “to appear, happen, show”). Compare Azerbaijani məruz.

parole.significato: petition, statement, (originally) a request submitted to a superior
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish معروضات (maruzat), plural of معروض (maruz), from Arabic مَعْرُوض (maʕrūḍ), passive participle of عَرَضَ (ʕaraḍa, “to appear, happen, show”). Formally the Arabic plural of maruz. Compare Azerbaijani məruzə.
From Ottoman Turkish مصال (masal), from older مثل (mesel), from Arabic مَثَل (maṯal). Doublet of mesel and metel; in Ottoman times this pronunciation became associated with less believable stories.
From Ottoman Turkish مصلحت (maslahat), from Arabic مَصْلَحَة (maṣlaḥa).
From Ottoman Turkish مصلاق (maslak), according to Tietze from Arabic مَسْلَك (maslak, “road, path”). See also موصلق (musluk).
From Ottoman Turkish مصرف, from Arabic مَصْرَف (maṣraf).
From Ottoman Turkish مصدر (masdar), from Arabic مَصْدَر (maṣdar).
From Ottoman Turkish معصوم (maʿsum), from Arabic مَعْصُوم (maʕṣūm, “protected”).
From Ottoman Turkish معصومیت (masumiyet), from Arabic مَعْصُومِيَّة (maʕṣūmiyya). by surface analysis, masum (“innocent”) + -iyet (“-ness,-hood”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مصون, from Arabic مَصُون (maṣūn), passive participle of صَانَ (ṣāna).

parole.significato: bobbin, spool, a cylinder or spindle around which threads, wires or cables are wound
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ماسوره (masura), from Arabic مَاسُورَة (māsūra, “bobbin, reel”), from the passive participle of the verb أَسَرَ (ʔasara, “to bind”).

parole.significato: canteen, water bottle, flask (Water container usually made of woolen fabric, leather or metal, used in travel or milita…
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مطره (matara, matare), from Arabic مَطَرَة (maṭara, “(leather) pouch, bag”).
From Ottoman Turkish مطبعه (matba'a), probably an Ottoman coinage from Arabic طَبَعَ (ṭabaʕa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مطبوع (matbû'), from Arabic مَطْبُوع (maṭbūʕ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مطبوعات (matbu'āt), from Arabic مَطْبُوعَات (maṭbūʕāt). By surface analysis, matbu + -at.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مأتم (maʼtem), from Arabic مَأْتَم (maʔtam, “mourning ceremony”).

parole.significato: borer, drill, gimlet, auger, any instrument used for drilling
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مثقب (miskab), from Arabic مِثْقَب (miṯqab, “drill”).

parole.significato: the first line of a qasida or ghazal
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مطلع (matla'), from Arabic مَطْلَع (maṭlaʕ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مطلوب (matlub), from Arabic مَطْلُوب (maṭlūb).
From Ottoman Turkish معطوف (matuf), from Arabic مَعْطُوف (maʕṭūf), passive participle of عَطَفَ (ʕaṭafa, “to incline, sympathize, be favorable to”).
From Ottoman Turkish ما واره, from Arabic مَا (mā) + وَرَاءَ (warāʔa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ماوی (mavi), from Arabic مَاوِيّ (māwiyy, “watery”).

parole.significato: parsley, any bright green, biennial herb of the species Petroselinum crispum
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish معدنوز (maydanoz), a medieval borrowing from Arabic مَعْدُونِس (maʕdūnis), from Byzantine Greek μακεδονήσιον (makedonḗsion, “parsley”). Doublet of bahteniz and bahdeniz, reborrowings found in southeastern dialects from the later Arabic form بَقْدُونِس (baqdūnis), and o
From Ottoman Turkish مایع, from Arabic مَائِع (māʔiʕ).

parole.significato: monkey, ape, primate, simian, any mammal in the order Primates except hominids
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish میمون (maymun, “monkey”), from Arabic مَيْمُون (maymūn, “baboon, mandrill”).

parole.significato: A valid justification that allows a mistake to be forgiven.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish معذرت (maʾẕeret, “a having an excuse, a valid excuse, an excuse, apology”), from Arabic مَعْذِرَة (maʕḏira, “excuse, forgiveness, pardon”), verbal noun of عَذَرَ (ʕaḏara, “to excuse”).
From Ottoman Turkish مزغل (mazgal), from Arabic مَزْغَل (mazḡal).
From Ottoman Turkish ماضی, from Arabic مَاضٍ (māḍin, “past”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مظلوم (mazlûm), from Arabic مَظْلُوم (maẓlūm).

parole.significato: One who has a valid excuse; excused.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish معذور (maʾẕur, “who has valid excuse, excusable”), from Arabic مَعْذُور (maʕḏūr), passive participle of عَذَرَ (ʕaḏara, “to excuse”).
From Ottoman Turkish مغاره (magare, mağara, “cave, cavern, pit”), from Arabic مَغَارَة (maḡāra), derived from غَار (ḡār).

From Ottoman Turkish مغدور (mağdur), from Arabic مَغْدُور (maḡdūr), passive participle of غَدَرَ (ḡadara, “to betray, desert”). Nişanyan considers this a pseudo-loan, a regular Arabic formation not attested in Arabic when it appeared in Ottoman Turkish in the 19th century.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مَغْفِرَت (mağfiret), from Arabic مَغْفِرَة (maḡfira).
From Ottoman Turkish مغفور (mağfur), from Arabic مَغْفُور (maḡfūr).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مغلوبيت, from Arabic مَغْلُوبِيَّة (maḡlūbiyya). By surface analysis, mağlup + -iyet.
From Ottoman Turkish مغلوب, from Arabic مَغْلُوب (maḡlūb, “defeated”), from غَلَبَ (ḡalaba, “to defeat, conquer”).
From Ottoman Turkish مغموم, from Arabic مَغْمُوم (maḡmūm).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مغرب (maġrib), from Arabic مَغْرِب (maḡrib).

parole.significato: interview (a formal meeting, in person, for the assessment of a candidate or applicant)

From Ottoman Turkish ملازم (mülazim), from Arabic مُلَازِم (mulāzim), active participle of لَازَمَ (lāzama). The original sense of persistence and inseparability evolved to mean an assistant.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مُلْغَیٰ (mülğâ), a late Ottoman borrowing from Arabic مُلْغًى (mulḡan), passive participle of أَلْغَى (ʔalḡā, “to cancel”).
From Ottoman Turkish ملحقات, plural of ملحق, from Arabic مُلْحَق (mulḥaq), passive participle of أَلْحَقَ (ʔalḥaqa). Formally, the Arabic plural of mülhak.

parole.significato: jute mallow, mulukhiyah, any annual herb of the species Corchorus olitorius, used as a vegetable
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ملوخیه (mülhiye, “jute mallow”), from Arabic مُلُوخِيَّة (mulūḵiyya, “jute mallow”), ultimately from the plural form of Ancient Greek μολόχιον (molókhion, “mallow”).

parole.significato: property (piece of land with a single owner)
parole.testo: From a confluence of Arabic مُلْك (mulk) and مِلْك (milk).
From Ottoman Turkish ملكیت (mülkiyet), from Arabic مِلْكِيَّة (milkiyya).
From Ottoman Turkish ملتجی (mülteci), from Arabic مُلْتَجِئ (multajiʔ), active participle of اِلْتَجَأَ (iltajaʔa). Despite the apparent suffix -ci, the entire word is from Arabic.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ملتفت (mültefit), from Arabic مُلْتَفِت (multafit).
From Ottoman Turkish ممانعت, from Arabic مُمَانَعَة (mumānaʕa), verbal noun of form III from the root م ن ع (m n ʕ).

From Ottoman Turkish منبت (münbit, mümbit), from Arabic مُنْبِت (munbit), from نَبَتَ (nabata, “to germinate, sprout, grow”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مناقشه, from Arabic مُنَاقَشَة (munāqaša).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مناظره (münâzare, münâzara), from Arabic مُنَاظَرَة (munāẓara).

From Ottoman Turkish مستملکه (müstemleke), from Arabic مُسْتَمْلَكَة (mustamlaka).

From Ottoman Turkish متاركه, from Arabic مُتَارَكَة (mutāraka).
From Ottoman Turkish متعدد (müteaddid), from Arabic مُتَعَدِّد (mutaʕaddid), active participle of تَعَدَّدَ (taʕaddada).

From Ottoman Turkish متعاقب (müteʿâkıb), from Arabic مُتَعَاقِب (mutaʕāqib).

parole.significato: A prayer recited by a muezzin before a funeral prayer or the call to prayer on an Eid or on Fridays.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سلف (selef), from Arabic سَلَف (salaf).
