From Ottoman Turkish تحلیف (tahlif), from Arabic تَحْلِيف (taḥlīf).
From Ottoman Turkish تحلیل (tahlil), from Arabic تَحْلِيل (taḥlīl), verbal noun of حَلَّلَ (ḥallala).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تخلیه (tahliye), from Arabic تَخْلِيَة (taḵliya), verbal noun of خَلَّى (ḵallā, “to leave, spare, set free”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تخمین (taḫmîn), from Arabic تَخْمِين (taḵmīn), verbal noun of خَمَّنَ (ḵammana).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تخمینا (taḫminā) or تخمیناً (taḫminen, “as an estimate, about”), from Arabic تَخْمِينًا (taḵmīnan) adverbial accusative of تَخْمِين (taḵmīn, “guess, speculation”), verbal noun of خَمَّنَ (ḵammana).
From Ottoman Turkish تخمینی (tahmini), from Arabic تَخْمِينِيّ (taḵmīniyy). By surface analysis, tahmin + -î.

parole.significato: In Divan literature, the situation of adding three lines to each couplet of a ghazal, pentameter.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تخمیس (tahmîs), from Arabic تَخْمِيس (taḵmīs).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تحمیص (tahmîs), from Arabic تَحْمِيص (taḥmīṣ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تحنیط, from Arabic تَحْنِيط (taḥnīṭ).

parole.significato: related to grinding or milling (grain, etc.)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish طحنیه (tahniye), probably a pseudo-Arabic coinage from Arabic طَحْن (ṭaḥn).
From Ottoman Turkish تخریبات (tahribat), from Arabic تَخْرِيبَات (taḵrībāt), plural of تَخْرِيب (taḵrīb) from which tahrip, tahrib.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تحریف (tahrîf), from Arabic تَحْرِيف (taḥrīf), verbal noun of حَرَّفَ (ḥarrafa, “to distort”).

parole.significato: An act of arousing sexual desire; excitation, stimulation.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تحریك (taḥrik, “a moving, causing to move or vibrate, inciting, impelling, instigating, a medicine's moving the bowels”), from Arabic تَحْرِيك (taḥrīk), verbal noun of حَرَّكَ (ḥarraka, “to move, to put in motion, to activate”). Cognates with Azerbaijani təhrik.
From Ottoman Turkish تخریب (tahrib), from Arabic تَخْرِيب (taḵrīb), verbal noun of خَرَّبَ (ḵarraba).
From Ottoman Turkish تحریر (tahrir), from Arabic تَحْرِير (taḥrīr), verbal noun of حَرَّرَ (ḥarrara).
From Arabic تَحْرِيرًا (taḥrīran), adverbial accusative of تَحْرِير (taḥrīr, “writing”). By surface analysis, tahrir (“writing”) + -en.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تحریری, from Arabic تَحْرِيرِيّ (taḥrīriyy).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تخریش (tahrîş), from Arabic تَخْرِيش (taḵrīš).

parole.significato: An act of collecting money, a debt, due etc.; collection.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تحصیل (taḥṣil, “a making be existent or present, producing, production; an extracting, educing; an obtaining, acquiring, acquisition, especially of learning or science; a collecting (money), collection of revenue”), from Arabic تَحْصِيل (taḥṣīl), verbal noun of حَصَّلَ
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تحصیلات, from Arabic تَحْصِيلَات (taḥṣīlāt), plural of تَحْصِيل (taḥṣīl). By surface analysis, tahsil + -at
From Ottoman Turkish تخصیص (tahsis), from Arabic تَخْصِيص (taḵṣīṣ).
From Ottoman Turkish تخصیصات (tahsisat), plural of تخصیص (tahsis), from Arabic تَخْصِيص (taḵṣīṣ), verbal noun of خَصَّصَ (ḵaṣṣaṣa, “to allocate, reserve”).
From Ottoman Turkish تحت (taht), from Arabic تَحْت (taḥt).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تحویل (tahvil), from Arabic تَحْوِيل (taḥwīl).
From Ottoman Turkish تاخل, from Arabic دَخْل (daḵl, “income”).

From Ottoman Turkish تحشیدات (tahşidat), Arabic plural of تحشید (tahşid), from Arabic تَحْشِيد (taḥšīd), verbal noun of حَشَدَ (ḥašada, “to gather, concentrate, mobilize”). Formally, the Arabic plural of obsolete tahşid, tahşit.

From Ottoman Turkish طاق (tak), from Arabic طَاق (ṭāq), possibly from Middle Persian *tāk, a variant of tʾg (/⁠tāg⁠/, “arch”) (compare modern Persian طاق (tâq, “arch”)). Doublet of taç (“crown; belt”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تقاص (taḳaṣ, “a mutually setting off claims against each other, to clear of indebtedness”), from Arabic تَقَاصّ (taqāṣṣ).
From Ottoman Turkish تقبیح, from Arabic تَقْبِيح (taqbīḥ), verbal noun of قَبَّحَ (qabbaḥa).
From Ottoman Turkish تقدیم (takdîm), from Arabic تَقْدِيم (taqdīm).
From Ottoman Turkish تقدیر (takdir), from Arabic تَقْدِير (taqdīr).

From Ottoman Turkish تعقیبات (takibat), in the form of a plural of تعقیب (takib), from Arabic تَعْقِيب (taʕqīb). In Ottoman times, persecution rather than prosecution, with تعقیبات قانونیه (literally “legal persecution”) for the legal sense.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تعقیب (taʿkîb), from Arabic تَعْقِيب (taʕqīb).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تاقیه or تقیه, from Arabic طَاقِيَّة (ṭāqiyya). Compare Turkmen tahýa, Uzbek taqya.
From Arabic تَقْلَع (taqlaʕ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تقلیدی, from Arabic تَقْلِيدِيّ (taqlīdiyy).
From Ottoman Turkish تقلید (taklid), from Arabic تَقْلِيد (taqlīd).
From Ottoman Turkish تقریبا (takriben), from Arabic تَقْرِيبًا (taqrīban), adverbial accusative of تَقْرِيب (taqrīb). By surface analysis, takrip + -en (adverbial suffix).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تقسیم, borrowed from Arabic تَقْسِيم (taqsīm), from قَسَّمَ (qassama).
From Ottoman Turkish تقسیط (taksit, “installment, dividend”), from Arabic تَقْسِيط (taqsīṭ), verbal noun of قَسَّطَ (qassaṭa, “to dispense, allot”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تقوی (takvâ), from Arabic تَقْوَى (taqwā, “piety”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تقویم (takvim, “a straightening, putting in proper order, showing the correct state of, the correct times or places of celestial phenomena etc. hence an almanac, a calendar”), from Arabic تَقْوِيم (taqwīm, “calendar”), verbal noun of قَوَّمَ (qawwama).

From Ottoman Turkish تقویه (takviye), from Arabic تَقْوِيَة (taqwiya), verbal noun of قَوَّى (qawwā). Ottoman Turkish also borrowed the alternative pronunciation تقویت (takviyet), but that form is obsolete.
From Ottoman Turkish طلبه, from Arabic طَلَبَة (ṭalaba), plural of طَالِب (ṭālib, “student”).
From Ottoman Turkish طلب (taleb), from Arabic طَلَب (ṭalab).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تالی (tāli, “that follows or goes behind, that succeeds”), from Arabic تَالٍ (tālin, “following, subsequent, next”), active participle of تَلَا (talā, “to follow, to walk behind another”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طالع (ṭaliʿ, “the ascendant in astrology, one's star, good luck”), from Arabic طَالِع (ṭāliʕ, “omen, luck”), from طَلَعَ (ṭalaʕa, “to appear”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تعلیم, borrowed from Arabic تَعْلِيم (taʕlīm), from عَلَّمَ (ʕallama).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تعلیمات (ta'lîmât), from Arabic تَعْلِيمَات (taʕlīmāt). By surface analysis, talim + -at.
From Ottoman Turkish طالب (talib), from Arabic طَالِب (ṭālib)
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تام (tam, “complete, exact; completely, exactly”), from Arabic تَامّ (tāmm).
From Ottoman Turkish تمام (tamam), from Arabic تَمَام (tamām).
From Ottoman Turkish تماماً (tamâmen), from Arabic تَمَامًا (tamāman), adverbial accusative of تَمَام (tamām). By surface analysis, tamam + -en (adverbial suffix).

parole.significato: repair, mending, reparation, restoration, the act of repairing or restoring something
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تعمیر (taʼmir, “repair, restoration”), from Arabic تَعْمِير (taʕmīr, “population; building, construction”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تعمیرات (taʼmirat), from Arabic تَعْمِيرَات (taʕmīrāt), plural of تَعْمِير (taʕmīr, “population; building, construction”). By surface analysis, tamir (“repair, restoration”) + -at.
From Ottoman Turkish تنور, from Arabic تَنُّور (tannūr).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طنین (tanin), from Arabic طَنِين (ṭanīn).
Calque of Arabic اللهُ أَكْبَر (allāhu ʔakbar).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طنطنه, from Arabic طَنْطَنَة (ṭanṭana, “twang, ringing, drum roll”). See the Ottoman Turkish entry for more.

parole.significato: organizing, putting in order; editing (a document)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish تنظیم (tanzîm), from Arabic تَنْظِيم (tanẓīm), verbal noun of نَظَّمَ (naẓẓama, “to organize, regulate, control”). Compare Azerbaijani tənzim.

parole.significato: side; one half (left or right, top or bottom, front or back, etc.) of something or someone.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طرف (“end; side, edge; vicinity; region”), ultimately from Arabic طَرَف (ṭaraf).
From Ottoman Turkish ترصد (tarassud), from Arabic تَرَصُّد (taraṣṣud), verbal noun of تَرَصَّدَ (taraṣṣada).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طرخون (tarhun), from Arabic طَرْخُون (ṭarḵūn), from Ancient Greek δρακόντιον (drakóntion).
From Arabic تَعْرِيف (taʕrīf).
From Ottoman Turkish تعرفه (ta'rife), an Ottoman alteration of Arabic تَعْرِيف (taʕrīf). The direct borrowing yielded tarif.

parole.significato: date (point of time at which a transaction or event takes place)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish تاریخ (tarih), from Arabic تَارِيخ (tārīḵ).
From Ottoman Turkish تاریخاً (tarihen), from Arabic تَارِيخًا (tārīḵan).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تاریخی (tarihi), from Arabic تَارِيخِيّ (tārīḵiyy). By surface analysis, tarih + -i (nisba suffix).
From Ottoman Turkish طریق (tarîk), from Arabic طَرِيق (ṭarīq).
From Ottoman Turkish طریقت (tarikat), from Arabic طَرِيقَة (ṭarīqa).
From Ottoman Turkish طرز (tarz), from Arabic طَرْز (ṭarz).

parole.significato: apologizing, the act of making an apology
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ﺗﺮضیه (tarziye, “pleasing, satisfying; apologizing”), from Arabic تَرْضِيَّة (tarḍiyya).

parole.significato: a bowl, typically made of metal.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish طاس (tas), which borrowed this from Arabic طَاس (ṭās, “bowl”) (a shortening of طَسْت (ṭast)), from Middle Persian tšt' (tašt), ultimately from the past participle of Proto-Iranian *taš- (“to make, construct; to cut”), from Proto-Indo-European *tetḱ-. Cognate with French tasse.
From Ottoman Turkish تصرف, from Arabic تَصَرُّف (taṣarruf).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تصوف (tasavvuf), from Arabic تَصَوُّف (taṣawwuf).
From Ottoman Turkish تصور (tasavvur), from Arabic تَصَوُّر (taṣawwur).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تصدیق (tasdîk), from Arabic تَصْدِيق (taṣdīq).

parole.significato: An act of clarifying, sorting out, refining.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تصفیه (taṣfiye, “a clearing, clarifying a liquid, a purifying from alloy or admixture, a cleaning or polishing, a making the heart or mind free from evil thoughts or intentions”), from Arabic تَصْفِيَة (taṣfiya, “clarifying, purifying”), verbal noun of صَفَا (ṣafā, “to
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تصحیح (tashîh), from Arabic تَصْحِيح (taṣḥīḥ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تصنیف, from Arabic تَصْنِيف (taṣnīf).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تصریف, from Arabic تَصْرِيف (taṣrīf).
From Ottoman Turkish تصویب (tasvib), from Arabic تَصْوِيب (taṣwīb), verbal noun of صَوَّبَ (ṣawwaba).
From Ottoman Turkish تصویر (tasvir), from Arabic تَصْوِير (taṣwīr).
From Ottoman Turkish تطبیق, from Arabic تَطْبِيق (taṭbīq), verbal noun of طَبَّقَ (ṭabbaqa, “to apply, cover”).

parole.significato: drill (an activity done as an exercise or practice, particularly in preparation for some possible future event or occur…
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish تطبیقات (tatbikat), from Arabic تَطْبِيقَات (taṭbīqāt), plural of تَطْبِيق (taṭbīq). By surface analysis, tatbik + -at.
From Ottoman Turkish تعطیل (ta'tīl), from Arabic تَعْطِيل (taʕṭīl).
From Ottoman Turkish تطمین (tatmin), from Arabic تَطْمِين (taṭmīn).
From Ottoman Turkish توسط (tevassut), from Arabic تَوَسُّط (tawassuṭ).
From Ottoman Turkish تعویض (ta'viz), from Arabic تَعْوِيض (taʕwīḍ), verbal noun of عَوَّضَ (ʕawwaḍa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish توصیف (tavsif), from Arabic تَوْصِيف (tawṣīf).
From Ottoman Turkish توصیه (tavsiye), from Arabic تَوْصِيَة (tawṣiya). See Azerbaijani tövsiyə.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طاووس, from Old Anatolian Turkish طاووس, from Arabic طَاوُوس (ṭāwūs), Aramaic טַוסָא (ṭawsā), from Ancient Greek τᾰώς (tăṓs). Compare Persian طاووس.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish توضیح, from Arabic تَوْضِيح (tawḍīḥ), verbal noun of وَضَّحَ (waḍḍaḥa).
From Ottoman Turkish طور (tavr, tavır, “manner; arrogance”), from Arabic طَوْر (ṭawr).
From Arabic طَائِفَة (ṭāʔifa, “troop”, “band”, “group”, “party”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تعیین (tayin), from Arabic تَعْيِين (taʕyīn), from عَيَّنَ (ʕayyana, “to appoint, designate”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طیر (tayr), from Arabic طَيْر (ṭayr).
From Ottoman Turkish تعظیم, from Arabic تَعْظِيم (taʕẓīm), verbal noun of عَظَّمَ (ʕaẓẓama).
From Arabic تَعْزِيَة (taʕziyya).
From Ottoman Turkish تضمینات (tazminat), borrowed from the plural of Arabic تَضْمِين (taḍmīn).
From Ottoman Turkish تضییق (tazyik), from Arabic تَضْيِيق (taḍyīq), verbal noun of ضَيَّقَ (ḍayyaqa). Compare Azerbaijani təzyiq (“pressure”).
From Ottoman Turkish تاج, from Arabic تَاج (tāj) or Persian تاج (tâj, “crown”). Doublet of tak (“arch, vault”).

parole.significato: change (the act of changing something into something else)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تغییر (tağyir), from Arabic تَغْيِير (taḡyīr).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تغشیش (tağşiş), from Arabic تَغْشِيش (taḡšīš).
From Ottoman Turkish تعادل (“becoming equal”), from Arabic تَعَادُل (taʕādul), verbal noun of تَعَادَلَ (taʕādala, “to be equal”).

parole.significato: subject; subjects (person or people ruled over)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تبعه (teba'a), from Arabic تَبَعَة (tabaʕa), plural of تَابِع (tābiʕ).
From Ottoman Turkish تبدیل (tebdil), from Arabic تَبْدِيل (tabdīl).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تبدل (tebeddül), from Arabic تَبَدُّل (tabaddul), verbal noun of تَبَدَّلَ (tabaddala).
From Ottoman Turkish تبسم (tebessüm), from Arabic تَبَسُّم (tabassum).
From Ottoman Turkish تبلیغات (tebligât), from Arabic تَبْلِيغ (tablīḡ).
From Ottoman Turkish تبلیغ (tebliğ), from Arabic تَبْلِيغ (tablīḡ), verbal noun of بَلَّغَ (ballaḡa), causative of بَلَغَ (balaḡa, “to reach, arrive”).
From Ottoman Turkish تجاوز (tecâvüz), from Arabic تَجَاوُز (tajāwuz).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تجدید (tecdîd), from Arabic تَجْدِيد (tajdīd), verbal noun of جَدَّدَ (jaddada).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تجدد (teceddüd), from Arabic تَجَدُّد (tajaddud), verbal noun of تَجَدَّدَ (tajaddada).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تجلی (tecellî), from Arabic تَجَلٍّ (tajallin).
From Ottoman Turkish تجسم (tecessüm) from Arabic تَجَسُّم (tajassum), verbal noun of تَجَسَّمَ (tajassama, “to become corporeal; to take form; to grow larger”).

parole.significato: A great interest to find out about something; curiosity, concern.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تجسس (tecessüs), from Arabic تَجَسُّس (tajassus).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تجرید (tecrîd), from Arabic تَجْرِيد (tajrīd), verbal noun of جَرَّدَ (jarrada). Compare Azerbaijani təcrid
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تجربه (tecrübe), from Arabic تَجْرِبَة (tajriba).

parole.significato: tajwid (rules governing pronunciation during recitation of the Qur'an.)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تجوید (tecvîd), from Arabic تَجْوِيد (tajwīd).
From Ottoman Turkish تداوی (tedâvi), from Arabic تَدَاوٍ (tadāwin).
From Ottoman Turkish تدبیر (tedbir), from Arabic تَدْبِير (tadbīr).
From Ottoman Turkish تدهیش (tedhiş, “bewilderment; terror”), from Arabic تَدْهِيش (tadhīš), from دَهِشَ (dahiša).
From Ottoman Turkish تأدیب (tedib), from Arabic تَأْدِيب (taʔdīb).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تدریجاً (tedricen), from Arabic تَدْرِيجًا (tadrījan) adverbial accusative of تَدْرِيج (tadrīj), verbal noun of دَرَّجَ (darraja, “to step forward, to proceed gradually”).By surface analysis, tedriç (“gradual progress”) + -en.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تدریجی (tedrîcî), from Arabic تَدْرِيجِيّ (tadrījiyy). By surface analysis, tedriç (“evolution”) + -i (nisba suffix).
From Ottoman Turkish تدریس (tedris), from Arabic تَدْرِيس (tadrīs), verbal noun of دَرَّسَ (darrasa, “to teach”).
From Ottoman Turkish تدویر (tedvir), from Arabic تَدْوِير (tadwīr).
From Ottoman Turkish تدویراً (tedviren), from Arabic تَدْوِيرًا (tadwīran).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تأهل (te’ehhül), from Arabic تَأَهُّل (taʔahhul).
From Ottoman Turkish تأسف, from Arabic تَأَسُّف (taʔassuf), verbal noun of تَأَسَّفَ (taʔassafa, “to feel sorry; to regret”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تأثر, from Arabic تَأَثُّر (taʔaṯṯur), verbal noun of تَأَثَّرَ (taʔaṯṯara, “to be influenced”). Cognate with Azerbaijani təəssür.
From Ottoman Turkish تفاوت (tefâvüt), from Arabic تَفَاوُت (tafāwut).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تفكر (tefekkür), from Arabic تَفَكُّر (tafakkur).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تفرعات (teferruat), plural of تفرع (teferru, “ramifying, subdivision”), from Arabic تَفَرُّع (tafarruʕ), verbal noun of تَفَرَّعَ (tafarraʕa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تفسخ (tefessüh), from Arabic تَفَسُّخ (tafassuḵ), verbal noun of تَفَسَّخَ (tafassaḵa).

From Ottoman Turkish تفرقه (tefrika, “dividing into sections; discord”), from Arabic تَفْرِقَة (tafriqa), verbal noun of فَرَّقَ (farraqa, “to separate”). The publishing or literary sense appeared in the 19th century and the older senses are obsolete in modern Turkish.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تفریط (tefrît), from Arabic تَفْرِيط (tafrīṭ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تفسیر (tefsîr), from Arabic تَفْسِير (tafsīr), verbal noun of فَسَّرَ (fassara, “to interpret”).

parole.significato: inspection (the act of examining something, often closely)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish تفتیش (teftiş), from Arabic تَفْتِيش (taftīš), verbal noun of فَتَّشَ (fattaša, “to inspect”).
From Ottoman Turkish تهاجم (tehacüm), from Arabic تَهَاجُم (tahājum), verbal noun of تَهَاجَمَ (tahājama, “to attack one another”).
From Ottoman Turkish تهجیر (tehcir), from Arabic تَهْجِير (tahjīr).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تهجد (teheccüd), from Arabic تَهَجُّد (tahajjud).
From Ottoman Turkish تهور (tehevvür), from Arabic تَهَوُّر (tahawwur).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تهیج (teheyyüç), from Arabic تَهَيُّج (tahayyuj, “agitation, irritation”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تأخیر (tehir), from Arabic تَأْخِير (taʔḵīr).
From Ottoman Turkish تهلكه (tehlike, tehlüke), from Arabic تَهْلِكَة (tahlika). Cognate with Crimean Tatar telüke.
From Ottoman Turkish تقابل, from Arabic تَقَابُل (taqābul).
From Ottoman Turkish تقاعد (tekaüd), from Arabic تَقَاعُد (taqāʕud), verbal noun of تَقَاعَدَ (taqāʕada, “to retire”).
From Ottoman Turkish تكبیر (tekbir), from Arabic تَكْبِير (takbīr).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تكبر (tekebbür, “pride, haughtiness; becoming proud and haughty”), from Arabic تَكَبُّر (takabbur).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تكلف (tekellüf), borrowed from Arabic تَكَلُّف (takalluf).
From Ottoman Turkish تكمل (tekemmül), from Arabic تَكَمُّل (takammul), verbal noun of تَكَمَّلَ (takammala, “to be or become whole, complete, perfect”).
From Ottoman Turkish تكرر, from Arabic تَكَرُّر (takarrur).

parole.significato: a Christian bey in Anatolia and Thrace during the Byzantine era
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish تكفور, from Arabic تَكْفُور (takfūr), from Middle Armenian թագւոր (tʻagwor), from Old Armenian թագաւոր (tʻagawor, “king”), from Parthian *tag(a)-bar (“king”, literally “crown bearing”), borrowed during the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia.
From Ottoman Turkish تأكید (tekid), from Arabic تَأْكِيد (taʔkīd), verbal noun of أَكَّدَ (ʔakkada).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تكلیف (teklif), borrowed from Arabic تَكْلِيف (taklīf), from كَلَّفَ (kallafa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تكرار (tekrar), from Arabic تَكْرَار (takrār).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تكثیر (teksîr), from Arabic تَكْثِير (takṯīr).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تكوین (tekvîn), from Arabic تَكْوِين (takwīn).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تكوین (tekvîn), from Arabic تَكْوِين (takwīn).
From Ottoman Turkish تكذیب, from Arabic تَكْذِيب (takḏīb), verbal noun of كَذَّبَ (kaḏḏaba, “to accuse of lying; to disbelieve”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تكافل, from Arabic تَكَافُل (takāful).
From Ottoman Turkish تكامل (tekamül), from Arabic تَكَامُل (takāmul).
From Ottoman Turkish تكاثف, from Arabic تَكَاثُف (takāṯuf), verbal noun of تَكَاثَفَ (takāṯafa, “to grow denser; to thicken”).
From Ottoman Turkish تلفظ (telaffuz), from Arabic تَلَفُّظ (talaffuẓ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تلافی, from Arabic تلافي.
From Ottoman Turkish تلقی (telakki, “receiving, accepting; interpretation”), from Arabic تَلَقٍّ (talaqqin), verbal noun of تَلَقَّى (talaqqā, “to receive, obtain”).
From Ottoman Turkish تلاش (telaş), from Arabic تَلَاشٍ (talāšin)
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تلف (telef), from Arabic تَلَف (talaf).
From Ottoman Turkish تالفات (telefat), plural of تلف (telef), from Arabic تَلَف (talaf).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تلقین, from Arabic تَلْقِين (talqīn).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دلال (dellâl), from Arabic دَلَّال (dallāl).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تماس, from Arabic تَمَاسّ (tamāss), verbal noun of تَمَاسَّ (tamāssa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تمایل, from Arabic تَمَايُل (tamāyul).
A 19th century borrowing from Arabic تَمَايُز (tamāyuz), verbal noun of تَمَايَزَ (tamāyaza, “to distinguish, differ”).
From Ottoman Turkish تنبیه, from Arabic تَنْبِيه (tanbīh).

parole.significato: An act of wishing for something to come true.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تمنی (temenni, “a desiring in one's heart and mind, an asking for, a requesting”), from Arabic تَمَنٍّ (tamannin), verbal noun of تَمَنَّى (tamannā, “to wish for, to desire”).
From Ottoman Turkish تمتع (temettü', “utilization”), from Arabic تَمَتُّع (tamattuʕ).
From Ottoman Turkish تأمین, from Arabic تَأْمِين (taʔmīn).
From Ottoman Turkish تامینات (te'minat), from Arabic تَأْمِينَات (taʔmīnāt).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تمیز (temiz), from Arabic تَمْيِيز (tamyīz). Doublet of temyiz.
From Ottoman Turkish تمكین (temkîn), from Arabic تَمْكِين (tamkīn).
From Ottoman Turkish تملیك (temlik), from Arabic تَمْلِيك (tamlīk), verbal noun of مَلَكَ (malaka, “to possess, take possession, control”).

From Ottoman Turkish تموز (temmuz), from Arabic تَمُّوز (tammūz), from Classical Syriac ܬܡܘܙ (tāmūz), from Aramaic תַּמּוּז (tāmuz), from Akkadian 𒌗𒋗 (ⁱᵗⁱDuʾzu/Dūzu), from Sumerian 𒌉𒍣 (DUMU.ZID, “the true son”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تمرین (temrîn), from Arabic تَمْرِين (tamrīn).
From Ottoman Turkish تمثیل (temsil), from Arabic تَمْثِيل (tamṯīl), verbal noun of مَثَلَ (maṯala, “to resemble, imitate, represent”).
From Ottoman Turkish تمثیلی (temsilî), from Arabic تَمْثِيلِيّ (tamṯīliyy). By surface analysis, temsil (“representation”) + -i (nisba suffix).
From Ottoman Turkish تمییز (temyiz), from Arabic تَمْيِيز (tamyīz). Doublet of temiz.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تناقض, from Arabic تَنَاقُض (tanāquḍ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تناسخ (tenasüh, “reincarnation”), from Arabic تناسخ (tanāsuḵ, “reincarnation”).

parole.significato: breeding, reproduction; spawning a new generation
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish تناسل (tenasül), from Arabic تَنَاسُل (tanāsul), verbal noun of تَنَاسَلَ (tanāsala).

parole.significato: A deep cooking pot, usually metallic.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تنجره (tencere, “a saucepan, kettle, stewpan, pipkin”), from Arabic طَنْجَرَة (ṭanjara).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تنفس (teneffüs), from Arabic تَنَفُّس (tanaffus).
From Ottoman Turkish تنزه (tenezzüh), from Arabic تَنَزُّه (tanazzuh).
From Ottoman Turkish تنزل (tenezzül), from Arabic تَنَزُّل (tanazzul), verbal noun of تَنَزَّلَ (tanazzala, “to descend; to drop”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تنقیط (tenkit), from Arabic تَنْقِيط (tanqīṭ).
From Ottoman Turkish تنویر, from Arabic تَنْوِير (tanwīr).

parole.significato: An act of declaring free from defect, absolving.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تنزیه (tenzih), from Arabic تَنْزِيه (tanzīh).
From Arabic تَنْزِيلَات (tanzīlāt). Compare Northern Kurdish tenzîlat.
From Ottoman Turkish ترقی (terakki), from Arabic تَرَقٍّ (taraqqin).
From Ottoman Turkish ترقیات, from Arabic تَرَقِّيَات (taraqqiyāt), plural of تَرَقٍّ (taraqqin), verbal noun of تَرَقَّى (taraqqā, “to progress”). Terakki comes from the singular.
From Ottoman Turkish تراكم (terâküm), from Arabic تَرَاكُم (tarākum).
From Ottoman Turkish تربیه (terbiye), from Arabic تَرْبِيَة (tarbiya)
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ترجیح (tercîh), from Arabic تَرْجِيح (tarjīḥ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ترجیحًا (tercîhen), derived from Arabic تَرْجِيحًا (tarjīḥan). By surface analysis, tercih (“preference”) + -en (“-ly”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ترجمان, from Arabic تَرْجُمَان (tarjumān), Classical Syriac ܬܰܪܓܡܳܢܳܐ (targmānā, “interpreter”), from Akkadian 𒅴𒁄 (targumannum, “interpreter”).
From Ottoman Turkish ترجمه (terceme, tercüme), from Arabic تَرْجَمَة (tarjama, “translation”).
From Ottoman Turkish تردد (tereddüd), from Arabic تَرَدُّد (taraddud).
From Ottoman Turkish ترفع, from Arabic تَرَفُّع (taraffuʕ), verbal noun of تَرَفَّعَ (taraffaʕa).
From Ottoman Turkish ترفیع (terfi), from Arabic تَرْفِيع (tarfīʕ), verbal noun of رَفَعَ (rafaʕa).
From Ottoman Turkish ترخیص (“permitting; permission, license”), from Arabic تَرْخِيص (tarḵīṣ), verbal noun of رَخَّصَ (raḵḵaṣa, “to allow”).
From Ottoman Turkish ترك (terk), from Arabic تَرْك (tark), verbal noun of تَرَكَ (taraka, “to leave, relinquish”).

parole.significato: An act of assembling, putting together, combining.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تركیب (terkib, “a mounting, a furnishing with arms and a mount, a joining or compounding together, a composite whole, compound, mixture”), from Arabic تَرْكِيب (tarkīb, “installation, putting up”), verbal noun of رَكَّبَ (rakkaba, “to assemble, to compose, to combine”)
From Ottoman Turkish ترتیب (tertip), from Arabic تَرْتِيب (tartīb).
From Ottoman Turkish تصادف (tesâdüf), from Arabic تَصَادُف (taṣāduf), verbal noun of تَصَادَفَ (taṣādafa, “to meet by chance”).

parole.significato: by chance, as a result of a coincidence, accidentally
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تصادفاً (tesādüfen), from Arabic تَصَادُفًا (taṣādufan) adverbial accusative of تَصَادُف (taṣāduf, “coincidence”), verbal noun of تَصَادَفَ (taṣādafa, “to meet by chance”). Compare Uzbek tasodifan, Uyghur تاسادىپەن (tasadipen) and Azerbaijani təsadüfən.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تساند (tesânüd), from Arabic تَسَانُد (tasānud).
From Ottoman Turkish تسجیل (tescil), from Arabic تَسْجِيل (tasjīl), verbal noun of سَجَّلَ (sajjala, “to register, to write down”), from Latin sigillum.
From Ottoman Turkish تسلی (teselli), from Arabic تَسَلٍّ (tasallin).

parole.significato: hijab, women dress with their heads covered.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تستر, from Arabic تَسَتُّر (tasattur).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تأثیر, from Arabic تَأْثِير (taʔṯīr).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تأسیس (te'sis), from Arabic تَأْسِيس (taʔsīs). Cognate with Persian تأسیس (ta'sīs /ta'sis), Uyghur تەسىس (tesis), and Uzbek taʼsis.
From Ottoman Turkish تأسیسات (te'sisat), Arabic plural of تأسیس (te'sis), from Arabic تَأْسِيس (taʔsīs).
From Ottoman Turkish تسعید (tesid), an Ottoman coinage based on Arabic سَعْد (saʕd).

parole.significato: An act of calming, soothing pain, anger, excitement etc.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تسكین (teskin, “a calming, pasifying, making quiet”), from Arabic تَسْكِين (taskīn, “pacification”), verbal noun of سَكَّنَ (sakkana, “to calm, to reassure, to appease”).
From Ottoman Turkish تسلیم (teslim), from Arabic تَسْلِيم (taslīm).
From Ottoman Turkish تثلیث (teslîs), from Arabic تَثْلِيث (taṯlīṯ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تسمیه (tesmiyye), borrowed from Arabic تَسْمِيَّة (tasmiyya).
From Ottoman Turkish تسبیح (tesbih), from Arabic تَسْبِيح (tasbīḥ, “praise, hymn”).
From Ottoman Turkish تثبیت (tesbit), from Arabic تَثْبِيت (taṯbīt), verbal noun of ثَبَّتَ (ṯabbata, “to make firm, stable; to confine, restrict”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تسویه (tesviye), from Arabic تَسْوِيَة (taswiya).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تتبع (tetebbu’), from Arabic تَتَبُّع (tatabbuʕ).
From Ottoman Turkish تدقیق (tedkik, “comminution”), from Arabic تَدْقِيق (tadqīq). The original sense of beating into slender form or grinding into fine particles is obsolete.

parole.significato: More than one thing suiting, coinciding with one another.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish توافق (tevāfuḳ, “a being or becoming in agreement with one another, agreement, correspondance”), from Arabic تَوَافُق (tawāfuq), verbal noun of تَوَافَقَ (tawāfaqa, “to agree with one another”).
From Ottoman Turkish توقف (tevakkuf), from Arabic تَوَقُّف (tawaqquf).
From Ottoman Turkish توارث (tevârüs), from Arabic تَوَارُث (tawāruṯ).
From Ottoman Turkish تواضع, from Arabic تَوَاضُع (tawāḍuʕ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish توجیه (tevcîh), from Arabic تَوْجِيه (tawjīh).

parole.significato: an act of turning, facing towards
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish توجه (teveccüh), from Arabic تَوَجُّه (tawajjuh).

parole.significato: in vain, pointlessly, to no purpose, for no good reason
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish توكللی (tevekküllü, tevekkeli) or توكلی (tevekkeli, “(originally) In reliance on God; trusting to chance, haphazardly”), from Arabic تَوَكُّل (tawakkul), verbal noun of تَوَكَّلَ (tawakkala, “to rely on, to trust entirely in, especially God”).
From Ottoman Turkish توكل (tevekkül), from Arabic تَوَكُّل (tawakkul), verbal noun of تَوَكَّلَ (tawakkala).
From Ottoman Turkish تولد, from Arabic تَوَلُّد (tawallud).

parole.significato: [with dative] undertaking, setting about, starting (a task)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish توسل (tevessül), from Arabic تَوَسُّل (tawassul).
From Ottoman Turkish توحید (tevhıd), from Arabic تَوْحِيد (tawḥīd).
From Ottoman Turkish توقیف (tevkıf), from Arabic تَوْقِيف (tawqīf).

parole.significato: appointing as an agent or attorney
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish توكیل, from Arabic تَوْكِيل (tawkīl), verbal noun of وَكَّلَ (wakkala, “to authorize, empower”).
From Ottoman Turkish تولید (tevlid), from Arabic تَوْلِيد (tawlīd).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish توسیع (tevsi), from Arabic تَوْسِيع (tawsīʕ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish توزیع (tevzî'), from Arabic تَوْزِيع (tawzīʕ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تیقظ (teyakkuz), borrowed from Arabic تيقّظ (“to be awake”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تیمم, from Arabic تَيَمُّم (tayammum).
From Ottoman Turkish تأیید (teʼyid, “corroborating; supporting”), from Arabic تَأْيِيد (taʔyīd), verbal noun of أَيَّدَ (ʔayyada, “to support, endorse, substantiate”).
From Ottoman Turkish تظاهر, from Arabic تَظَاهُر (taẓāhur), verbal noun of تَظَاهَرَ (taẓāhara, “to manifest, display, exhibit”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تظاهرات (tezahürat), plural of تظاهر (tezahür), from Arabic تَظَاهُر (taẓāhur).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تضاد (teżad, teżat, “a being or becoming opposed to, contrary to, or repugnant to one another, mutual opposition, contrariety, an antithesis”), from Arabic تَضَادّ (taḍādd), verbal noun of تَضَادَّ (taḍādda, “to be opposed to one another, to be contradictory, to contra
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تذلل (tezellül), from Arabic تَذَلُّل (taḏallul).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تزوج (tezevvüc), from Arabic تَزَوُّج (tazawwuj).
From Ottoman Turkish تذهیب (tezhîb), from Arabic تَذْهِيب (taḏhīb).
From Ottoman Turkish تذكره (tezkire, tezkere), from Arabic تَذْكِرَة (taḏkira).

parole.significato: An act of humiliating, disgracing, looking down on.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تذلیل (teẕlil, “a making to be submissive and humble”), from Arabic تَذْلِيلْ (taḏlīl), verbal noun of ذَلَّلَ (ḏallala, “to degrade, to make humble, to defeat, to overpower”).
From Ottoman Turkish تزیینات (tezyinat), plural of تزیین (tezyin), from Arabic تَزْيِين (tazyīn).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تجهیز (techiz), from Arabic تَجْهِيز (tajhīz).
From Ottoman Turkish تجهیزات (techizat), from Arabic تَجْهِيزَات (tajhīzāt).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تشبیه (teşbih), from Arabic تَشْبِيه (tašbīh).
From Ottoman Turkish تثدید (teşdid), from Arabic تَشْدِيد (tašdīd).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تشبث, from Arabic تَشَبُّث (tašabbuṯ), verbal noun of تَشَبَّثَ (tašabbaṯa, “to be stubborn”).
From Ottoman Turkish تشكل, from Arabic تَشَكُّل (tašakkul), verbal noun of تَشَكَّلَ (tašakkala, “to become shaped, formed”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تشكر (teşekkür), from Arabic تَشَكُّر (tašakkur).
Plural of the noun teşekkür that is also seen in teşekkür ederim, from Arabic تَشَكُّر (tašakkur), from the triconsonantal root ش ك ر (š k r), to thank, to be grateful.

parole.significato: honor (especially the one felt when meeting someone)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تشرف (teşerrüf), from Arabic تَشَرُّف (tašarruf).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تشوش (teşevvüş), from Arabic تَشَوُّش (tašawwuš, “disorder, confusion, chaos”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تشهیر (teşhir), borrowed from Arabic تَشْهِير (tašhīr), from شَهَّرَ (šahhara).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تشخیص (teşhıs), from Arabic تَشْخِيص (tašḵīṣ).
From Ottoman Turkish تشكیل (teşkil), from Arabic تَشْكِيل (taškīl), verbal noun of شَكَّلَ (šakkala).
From Ottoman Turkish تشكیلات, from Arabic تَشْكِيلَات (taškīlāt), plural of تَشْكِيل (taškīl, “organization”). By surface analysis, teşkil + -at.

parole.significato: extension, the act of extending or enlarging in length, breadth, or scope
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تشمیل (teşmil, “covering; making haste”), from Arabic تَشْمِيل (tašmīl, “including, enclosing”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تَشْرِیف (teşrîf), from Arabic تَشْرِيف (tašrīf).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تشریح (teşrih) from Arabic تَشْرِيح (tašrīḥ).
From Ottoman Turkish تشریك (teşrik), from Arabic تَشْرِيك (tašrīk), form II verbal noun from ش ر ك (š r k).

parole.significato: Either of two months of the solar year.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish تشرین, from Arabic تشرين (tišrīn). Compare Hebrew תִּשְׁרֵי (tishréi).

parole.significato: October (tenth month of the Gregorian and Julian calendars)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish تشرین أول (teşrin-i evvel), from Arabic تِشْرِين الْأَوَّل (tišrīn al-ʔawwal), equivalent to teşrin + evvel. The name was officially changed to Ekim by law number 4696 passed January 10, 1945.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تشرین ثانی (teşrin-i sani), from Arabic تِشْرِين الثَانِي (tišrīn aṯ-ṯānī); equivalent to teşrin + sani (“second”). The name was officially changed to kasım by law number 4696 passed January 10, 1945.
From Ottoman Turkish تشویق, from Arabic تَشْوِيق (tašwīq).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تشویش (teşviş), from Arabic تَشْوِيش (tašwīš, “muddling, blurring”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تجارت (ticâret, “trade, commerce; profit”), from Arabic تِجَارَة (tijāra, “commerce, trade”), verbal noun of تَجَرَ (tajara, “to trade, to traffic, to practice commerce”).
From Arabic تِجَارِيّ (tijāriyy). Compare the noun ticaret from تِجَارَة (tijāra).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تلاوت (tilavet), from Arabic تِلَاوَة (tilāwa).
From Arabic تِمْسَاح (timsāḥ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تین, from Arabic تِين (tīn).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طوپ یكون (top yekûn, “a sum total”), from طوپ (top) and Arabic يَكُنْ (yakun), from كَانَ (kāna, “to be, to exist”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طوفان (tufan), from Arabic طُوفَان (ṭūfān), itself from a Sinitic language (cfr. Cantonese 大風 /大风 (daai⁶ fung¹)). Doublet of tayfun.

From Ottoman Turkish تحاف (tuhaf), from Arabic تُحَف (tuḥaf), plural of تُحْفة (tuḥfa, “something precious, treasure”), also used in a figurative sense, including of a precious, i.e. curious and unusual, story or anecdote.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تحفه, from Arabic تحفة.
From Ottoman Turkish طلوع, from Arabic طُلُوع (ṭulūʕ), verbal noun of طَلَعَ (ṭalaʕa).

parole.significato: The first to grow at the start of the season; very fresh.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ترفنده (türfende) or طرفانده (turfanda), further etymology is uncertain. Theories include; * Related to Arabic طُرْفَة (ṭurfa, “novelty, rarity”), * Derived from the name of the city Turfan, which is famous for high quality fresh fruits and vegetables, * Derived from P
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تهمت, from Arabic تُهْمَة (tuhma).
From Ottoman Turkish توبه (tevbe), from Arabic تَوْبَة (tawba).
From Arabic تُجَّار (tujjār, “merchants, businessmen”), plural of تَاجِر (tājir) whence the synonym tacir.
From tüm + -ce, a partial calque of Arabic جُمْلَة (jumla). Coined by Turkish Language Association to replace cümle.
From Ottoman Turkish تربه (türbe), from Arabic تُرْبَة (turba).

parole.significato: Letter of the Arabic alphabet: ط
parole.testo: From Arabic طَاء (ṭāʔ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طبی (tıbbî), from Arabic طِبِّيّ (ṭibbiyy). By surface analysis, tıp (“medicine”) + -i (nisba suffix).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طفل (tıfl), from Arabic طِفْل (ṭifl).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طلسم (tılsım), borrowed from Arabic طِلَسْم (ṭilasm), borrowed from Ancient Greek τέλεσμα (télesma, “payment”), from τελέω (teléō, “to pay”) + -μα (-ma).
From Ottoman Turkish طب (tıbb), from Arabic طِبّ (ṭibb).

parole.significato: An exact match of a thing, its identical copy.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طبقی (ṭıbḳı), from Arabic طِبْقًا (ṭibqan), adverbial accusative of طِبْق (ṭibq, “thing that matches in form”), it is uncertain if it is derived with the Arabic ـِيّ (-iyy, nisba suffix) or Turkish -ı (possessive suffix).
From Ottoman Turkish اعجوبه (uʾcube, “wonder, an unusual thing”), from Old Anatolian Turkish اعجوبه (üʾcūbe), from Arabic أُعْجُوبَة (ʔuʕjūba, “wonder”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish افقی (ufuki), from Arabic أُفُقِيّ (ʔufuqiyy). By surface analysis, ufuk (“horizon”) + -i (nisba suffix).
From Ottoman Turkish افق, from Arabic أُفُق (ʔufuq).
Derived from Ottoman Turkish اخروی (uhrevî), from Arabic أُخْرَوِيّ (ʔuḵrawiyy).
From Ottoman Turkish اخوت (uhuvvet), from Arabic أُخُوَّة (ʔuḵuwwa).

From Arabic أُمُور (ʔumūr).

parole.significato: element (one of the simplest or essential parts or principles)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish عنصر (unsur), from Arabic عُنْصُر (ʕunṣur).

parole.significato: sap, juice of a plant or fruit
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish عصاره (usare), borrowed from Arabic عُصَارَة (ʕuṣāra).

parole.significato: astrolabe, an astronomical and navigational instrument for gauging the altitude of the Sun and stars
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اسطرلاب (usturlab, “astrolabe”), from Arabic أَسْطُرْلَاب (ʔasṭurlāb), from Ancient Greek ἀστρολάβος (astrolábos).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اصول (usul), from Arabic اُصُول (uṣūl), plural of أَصْل (ʔaṣl).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish وعد (vaad), from Arabic وَعْد (waʕd).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish وعظ (vaʼz), from Arabic وَعْظ (waʕẓ).

From Ottoman Turkish واعظ (vâiz), from Arabic وَاعِظ (wāʕiẓ).

parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish والله (vallahi), from Arabic وَاللهِ (wallāhi, “by God”).
From Ottoman Turkish واردات (varidat), from Arabic وَارِدَات (wāridāt, “imports; receipts, proceeds”), plural of وَارِد (wārid, “arrival”). Formally, the Arabic plural of varit.
From Arabic وَسَط (wasaṭ).
From Ottoman Turkish واسع (vasi), from Arabic وَاسِع (wāsiʕ).
From Ottoman Turkish وصی (“testator; executor, trustee”), from Arabic وَصِيّ (waṣiyy), from و ص ي (w ṣ y).

parole.significato: will (a legal document that states who is to receive a person’s estate and assets after their death)

From Ottoman Turkish وظیفه (vazife, vazıfa), from Arabic وَظِيفَة (waẓīfa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish وضعیت (vazʼiyet), from Arabic وَضْعِيَّة (waḍʕiyya).
From Ottoman Turkish واضح (vazıh), from Arabic وَاضِح (wāḍiḥ).
From Ottoman Turkish و (ve), from Arabic وَ (wa).

parole.significato: plague (disease caused by Yersinia pestis; any outbreak of pestilence)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish وبا (veba), from Arabic وَبَاء (wabāʔ, “epidemic”).

parole.significato: A moral responsibility that can lead to sin, a burden on one's conscience and punishment in the afterlife.

parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ولیعهد (veliahd), from Arabic وَلِيّ عَهْد (waliyy ʕahd).

parole.significato: Someone who does a favor of immesurable importance for someone.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ولی نعمت (veli niʿmet, “a benefactor”), from Arabic وَلِيّ اَلنِّعْمَة (waliyy an-niʕma), from وَلِيّ (waliyy, “helper, protector, benefactor, patron”) + نِعْمَة (niʕma, “blessing, benefit”), equivalent to veli + nimet. Compare Uzbek valineʼmat, vallamat.
From Ottoman Turkish وراثت (verâset), from Arabic وِرَاثَة (wirāṯa).

parole.significato: tuberculosis, consumption, phthisis, an infectious disease caused by a species of mycobacterium
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ورم (verem, “tumor; tubercolosis”), from Arabic وَرَم (waram, “tumor”).
From Ottoman Turkish و سائره (ve sâire, literally “and others”), from Arabic وَ (wa-, “and”) and سَائِرَة (sāʔira, “others”, inanimate plural).
From Ottoman Turkish وصایت (vesâyet), from Arabic وِصَايَة (wiṣāya).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish وثیقه (vesika), from Arabic وَثِيقَة (waṯīqa).
From Ottoman Turkish وسیله (vesile), from Arabic وَسِيلَة (wasīla).

parole.significato: that's that, end of story, period
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish والسلام (vesselâm), from the Arabic phrase وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللّٰهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ (wa-s-salāmu ʕalaykum wa-raḥmatu llāhi wa-barakātuhu, “May the peace, mercy, and blessing of God be upon you!”), a phrase used at the end of speeches, especially Islamic
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish وسوسه (vesvese), from Arabic وَسْوَسَة (waswasa).

From Ottoman Turkish وزن, from Arabic وَزْن (wazn).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish وزیر (vezir), from Arabic وَزِير (wazīr).

parole.significato: kind of balance used to measure weights
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish وزنه (vezne, “kind of balance”), itself from Arabic وَزْنَة (wazna, “a particular weight”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish وجدان (vicdan, “conscience”), from Arabic وِجْدَان (wijdān).
From Ottoman Turkish ولایت (vilâyet), from Arabic وِلَايَة (wilāya).
From Ottoman Turkish وقوع (vuku, “event; fall”), from Arabic وُقُوع (wuqūʕ), verbal noun of وَقَعَ (waqaʕa).

parole.significato: reunion, especially a long-awaited or spiritual one

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ظن, from Arabic ظَنّ (ẓann).

parole.significato: A trade performed mainly for material needs requiring experience, skill of hand and mastery; handicraft.

From Ottoman Turkish ضبط (zabt), from Arabic ضَبْط (ḍabṭ).

From Ottoman Turkish ذلیل (zelil), from Arabic ذَلِيل (ḏalīl).
From Ottoman Turkish زلزله (zelzele, zerzele), from Arabic زَلْزَلَة (zalzala).

parole.significato: bag with handles woven from straw or thatch
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish زنبیل (zembil, “basket”), itself from Arabic زَبِّيل (zabbīl, “frail, basket”).

parole.testo: A vulgar form of Ottoman Turkish زمهریر (zemherir), from Arabic زَمْهَرِير (zamharīr).

From Ottoman Turkish ذره (zerre), from Arabic ذَرَّة (ḏarra).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زراعی (zirâ'î), from Arabic زِرَاعِيّ (zirāʕiyy).

parole.significato: mountaintop, peak, summit, head, pinnacle, the highest point of a mountain, hill, or similar geographical feature
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ذروه (zirve, “mountaintop, summit”), from Arabic ذِرْوَة (ḏirwa, “uppermost part, vertex, summit”).
From Ottoman Turkish ضیا (zıya), from Arabic ضِيَاء (ḍiyāʔ).
From Ottoman Turkish زیاده (ziyade, “many, much, more, too much; great”), from Arabic زِيَادَة (ziyāda).
From Ottoman Turkish ضیافت (zıyâfet, ziyâfet), from Arabic ضِيَافَة (ḍiyāfa), verbal noun of ضَافَ (ḍāfa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زیارت (ziyâret), borrowed from Arabic زِيَارَة (ziyāra).
From Ottoman Turkish زینت, borrowed from Arabic زِينَة (zīna).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ظلم, borrowed from Arabic ظُلْم (ẓulm).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ذو, from Arabic ذُو (ḏū).

parole.significato: venereal (related to diseases of the genitals)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish زهروی (zührevi), adjective form of Arabic زُهْرَة (zuhra, “Venus”); perhaps a calque of French vénérien. Attested since at least 1873.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زكام (zükâm), from Arabic زُكَام (zukām).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ذل (ẕüll, “submissiveness, degradation, weakness, a low estate, abjectness”), from Arabic ذُلّ (ḏull, “lowness, baseness, vileness, abjectness”), verbal noun of ذَلَّ (ḏalla, “to be low, to be humble”).
From Ottoman Turkish زمره, from Arabic زُمْرَة (zumra).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زرافه (zürafa), from Arabic زَرَافَة (zarāfa), from Classical Syriac ܙܪܢܦܐ (zarnāp̄ā), from Classical Persian زُرنَاپَا (zurnāpā). Etymologically related to zurna and piyade.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ذریت (zürriyet, “progeny, stock”), itself from Arabic ذُرِّيَّة (ḏurriyya).

parole.significato: Letter of the Arabic alphabet: ظ
parole.testo: From Arabic ظَاء (ẓāʔ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ضدیت (zıddiyet), from Arabic ضِدِّيَّة (ḍiddiyya). By surface analysis, zıt + -iyet
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زقوم, from Arabic زَقُّوم (zaqqūm). Doublet of zakkum.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زندیق (zındık), from Arabic زِنْدِيق (zindīq).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ضد (żıd, żıt, “a contrary, an opposite, opposition”), from Arabic ضِدّ (ḍidd, “opposite, contrast”), from تَضَادَّ (taḍādda, “to be opposed to one another, to be contradictory, to contradict one another”).
From Ottoman Turkish عاجز (aciz), from Arabic عَاجِز (ʕājiz).
From Ottoman Turkish عادت ('adet), from Arabic عَادَة (ʕāda, “custom”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish عادتا (“usually, customarily; simply, merely; in fact, really”), from Arabic (adverb) عادةً (ʕādatan). By surface analysis, âdet + -en.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish عاقد, from Arabic عَاقِد (ʕāqid)
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish عالم (alem), borrowed from Arabic عَالَم (ʕālam), borrowed from Aramaic עָלְמָא / ܥܳܠܡܳܐ (ʿāləmā).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish عالم (ālim, “who knows, learned, erudite, a doctor of science”), from Arabic عَالِم (ʕālim).

parole.significato: fine, good, nice, excellent, superb, splendid
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اعلی (aʿlâ), from Arabic أَعْلَى (ʔaʕlā, literally “higher, highest”). Compare Azerbaijani əla.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آمین, borrowed from Arabic آمِينَ (ʔāmīna), borrowed from Classical Syriac ܐܰܡܺܝܢ (ʾāmēn) or Aramaic אַמִין (ʾāmēn).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اعمی, from Arabic أَعْمَى (ʔaʕmā).
From Ottoman Turkish عاشق (aşık), from Arabic عَاشِق (ʕāšiq).
From Ottoman Turkish عمر, from Arabic عُمْر (ʕumr).

parole.significato: custom, usage (long-established practice, considered as unwritten law, and resting for authority on long consent)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish عرف (ürf), from Arabic عُرْف (ʕurf).

parole.significato: conventional, customary (in accordance with, or established by, custom or common usage)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish عرفی (ürfi), from Arabic عُرْفِيّ (ʕurfiyy).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish عُذْر (ʻözr, ʻözür), from Arabic عُذْر (ʕuḏr). See also Classical Persian عُذْر (ʻuḏr) and Azerbaijani üzr.
From Ottoman Turkish اجرت (ücret), from Arabic أُجْرَة (ʔujra).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish الفت (ülfet), from Arabic أُلْفَة (ʔulfa).
From Ottoman Turkish امت (ümmet), from Arabic أُمَّة (ʔumma).
From Ottoman Turkish عمران, from Arabic عُمْرَان (ʕumrān).
From ün (“reputation, voice”) + -süz (“-less”). Calque of Arabic صَامِت (ṣāmit).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish عنوان (ʼunvan, “title”), from Arabic عُنْوَان (ʕunwān).
From Ottoman Turkish اس (üss, üs), from Arabic أُسّ (ʔuss).

parole.significato: wording, way of choosing words speaking or writing
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اسلوب, from Arabic أُسْلُوب (ʔuslūb).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اسطوانه, استوانه, from Arabic أُسْطُوَانَة (ʔusṭuwāna), from Aramaic אִיסְטְוָונָא (ʾesṭwānā, “column, pillar”) ultimately from Middle Persian [script needed] (stwn' /⁠stūn⁠/, “column, pillar”). Doublet of sütun, derived from New Persian.

parole.significato: one of the tones in the makam system, used in Turkish classical music, resembling the low F note
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish عراق (ʼırak), from Arabic عِرَاق (ʕirāq, “Iraq”).

parole.significato: race (a large group of people set apart from others on the basis of a common heritage)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish عرق ('ırk), from Arabic عِرْق (ʕirq).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish عرض (ırz), from Arabic عِرْض (ʕirḍ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اسقاط (iskât), from Arabic إِسْقَاط (ʔisqāṭ).
From Ottoman Turkish اصلاح (ıslah), from Arabic إِصْلَاح (ʔiṣlāḥ).
From Ottoman Turkish اصلاحات, from Arabic إِصْلَاحَات (ʔiṣlāḥāt).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اصرار, from Arabic إِصْرَار (ʔiṣrār).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اصطفاء (ıstıfa), from Arabic اِصْطِفَاء (iṣṭifāʔ, “selecting; selection”)
From Ottoman Turkish اصطلاح (ıstılah), from Arabic اِصْطِلَاح (iṣṭilāḥ). Compare Azerbaijani istilah.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish عطریات (ıtriyat), from Arabic عِطْرِيَّة (ʕiṭriyya).
From Ottoman Turkish اضطرار (ıztırar, ızdırar), from Arabic اِضْطِرَار (iḍṭirār).

parole.significato: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic calendar)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish شعبان (şaban), from Arabic شَعْبَان (šaʕbān).

parole.significato: dawn, or the light just before daybreak
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شفق (şefak, şafak), from Arabic شَفَق (šafaq, “twilight, dusk”). The meaning shifted from dusk to dawn in Ottoman times.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شهاب (şihab, şahab), from Arabic شِهَاب (šihāb).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شاهقه (şahika), feminine form of شاهق (şahik, “towering, lofty”), from Arabic شَاهِق (šāhiq, “towering, lofty”).
From Ottoman Turkish شاهد (şahid), from Arabic شَاهِد (šāhid).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شخصاً (şahsan), from Arabic شَخْصًا (šaḵṣan), adverbial accusative of شَخْص (šaḵṣ, “person, individual”). By surface analysis, şahıs + -en.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شخصی, from Arabic شَخْصِيّ (šaḵṣiyy). By surface analysis, şahıs (“person”) + -i (nisba suffix).
From Ottoman Turkish شخصیت (şahsiyet), from Arabic شَخْصِيَّة (šaḵṣiyya).
From Ottoman Turkish شخص (şahs), from Arabic شَخْص (šaḵṣ).
From Ottoman Turkish شائبه (şaibe), from Arabic شَائِبَة (šāʔiba).
From Ottoman Turkish شاعر, from Arabic شَاعِر (šāʕir).
From Ottoman Turkish شاعره, from Arabic شَاعِرَة (šāʕira). By surface analysis, şair + -e.
From Ottoman Turkish شاقه, شقا (şaka, “fun, joke”), further origin unknown. May be an ironic derivation of Arabic شَقَاء (šaqāʔ, “unhappiness”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شقاق, from Arabic شِقَاق (šiqāq).
From Ottoman Turkish شقی (şakı), from Arabic شَقِيّ (šaqiyy, “miserable; villain”). The original sense, miserable, became obsolete before modern Turkish. From the same root as şaka.

parole.significato: apple melon, a fragrant but tasteless melon of the variety Cucumis melo var. dudaim
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شمامه (şemame, şemama), from Arabic شَمَّامَة (šammāma).

parole.significato: reputation, the worth or estimation in which something or someone is held
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شان (şan), from Old Anatolian Turkish شان (şān), from Arabic شَأْن (šaʔn)
From Ottoman Turkish شانلی (şanlı), from Arabic شَأْن (šaʔn), equivalent to şan + -lı.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شاب (şab), from Arabic شَبّ (šabb, “vitriol; alum”).
From Ottoman Turkish شراب (şarab), from Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (şarab, “wine”), from Arabic شَرَاب (šarāb). Cognate with Gagauz şarap.

parole.significato: East (preserved in some compounds, where a historical sense is preferable)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish شرق (şark), from Arabic شَرْق (šarq).
From Ottoman Turkish شرقی (şarki), from Arabic شَرْقِيّ (šarqiyy). Equivalent to şark (“orient, east”) + -i (nisba suffix). Compare Azerbaijani şərqi.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شطفات, from Arabic شطف.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شبابت (şebabet), from Arabic شَبَابَة (šabāba).
From Ottoman Turkish شبكه, from Arabic شَبَكَة (šabaka).

From Ottoman Turkish شجره (şecere, “tree, bush; family tree, pedigree”), from Arabic شَجَرَة (šajara), singulative of شَجَر (šajar, “trees”). Cognate with Azerbaijani şəcərə, Bashkir шәжәрә (şäjärä), Kazakh шежіре (šejire), Kyrgyz санжыра (sanjıra), Uzbek shajara, etc.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شفاعت (şefaat), from Arabic شَفاعَة (šafāʕa).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شفاف (şeffaf, “transparent”), from Arabic شَفَّاف (šaffāf).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شفقت (şefkat, şafkat), from Arabic شَفَقَة (šafaqa).

parole.significato: the property or state of being a witness
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شهادت (şehâdet), from Arabic شَهَادَة (šahāda).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شهید (şehid), from Arabic شَهِيد (šahīd).

parole.significato: of a bluish or light grey color
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شهلا (şehla), from Arabic شَهْلَاء (šahlāʔ), feminine singular of أَشْهَل (ʔašhal). Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شهوانی (şehvāni), from Arabic شَهْوانِيّ (šahwāniyy).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شهوت (şehvet), from Arabic شَهْوَة (šahwa).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شكلی (şeklî), from Arabic شَكْلِيّ (šakliyy). By surface analysis, şekil (“form”) + -i (nisba suffix).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شكوی (şekva, “complaint”), from Arabic شَكْوَى (šakwā, “complaint”)

parole.significato: waterfall, falls, cascade, cataract, a flow of water over the edge of a cliff
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شلاله (şelale), from Arabic شَلَّالَة (šallāla), variant of شَلَّال (šallāl, “waterfall”), a word of Aramaic origin.
From Ottoman Turkish شمع, from Arabic شَمْع (šamʕ). Compare Azerbaijani şəm, şam.
From Ottoman Turkish شماتت (şematet), from Arabic شَمَاتَة (šamāta), doublet of şamata.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شمس, borrowed from Arabic شَمْس (šams), from Proto-Semitic *śamš-.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شمسیه, borrowed from Arabic شَمْسِيَّة (šamsiyya)., with semantic shift. By surface analysis, şems + -iye.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شمسی, from Arabic شَمْسِيّ (šamsiyy), from شَمْس (šams, “sun”) + ـِيّ (-iyy). By surface analysis, şems (“sun”) + -î (nisba suffix).
From Ottoman Turkish شر, from Arabic شَرّ (šarr).
From Ottoman Turkish شرع, from Arabic شَرْع (šarʕ).

parole.significato: relating to Islamic law or Sharia
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شرعی, from Arabic شَرْعِيّ (šarʕiyy). By surface analysis, şer (“law”) + -i (nisba suffix).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شراره (şerare), from Arabic شَرَارَة (šarāra, “spark”).
From Ottoman Turkish شرف, from Arabic شَرَف (šaraf).
From Arabic شَرَّفَ (šarrafa, “to be noble, illustrious”).

parole.significato: gallery of a minaret, where the call to prayer is given
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish شرفه (şerefe), from Arabic شُرْفَة (šurfa, “veranda, balcony, battlement”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شرح (şerh) from Arabic شَرْح (šarḥ).
From Ottoman Turkish شریعت (şeri'at), from Arabic شَرِيعَة (šarīʕa, literally “way”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شریف (şerif, “noble; holy, sacred”), from Arabic شَرِيف (šarīf).
From Ottoman Turkish شریك (şerik), from Arabic شَرِيك (šarīk).

parole.significato: tape, strip, band, ribbon, any thin and flat material produced in the form of a roll
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شریت (şerit), from Arabic شَرِيط (šarīṭ, “tape, ribbon, band”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شرج (şerc, “anus”), from Arabic شَرْج (šarj).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شوق (şevk, “a longing desire, ardent yearning, ardor, eagerness”) from Arabic شَوْق (šawq, “longing, yearning, missing”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شوكت (şevket), from Arabic شَوْكَة (šawka).

parole.significato: Shawwal (the tenth month of the Islamic calendar)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شوال (şevval), from Arabic شَوَّال (šawwāl).
From Ottoman Turkish شی, شیئ (şey, “thing”), ultimately from Arabic شَيْء (šayʔ). For the "penis" sense development, compare Azerbaijani şey and Armenian բան (ban).
From Ottoman Turkish شیخ (şeyh), from Arabic شَيْخ (šayḵ).
From Ottoman Turkish شیطان (şeytan), from Old Anatolian Turkish شیطان (şeytān), from Arabic شَيْطَان (šayṭān).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شیطانی, from Arabic شَيْطَانِيّ (šayṭāniyy). By surface analysis, şeytan + -i.

parole.significato: strength, intensity, the degree of a power, force, or motion
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شدت (şiddet), from Arabic شِدَّة (šidda, “strenght, severity, violence”).
From Ottoman Turkish شفا (şifâ), from Arabic شِفَاء (šifāʔ, “healing, recovery”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شیعی (şîʿî), from Arabic شِيعِيّ (šīʕiyy). By surface analysis, Şia + -i.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شعر, from Arabic شِعْر (šiʕr).

parole.significato: complaint, plaint, grouse, grievance, a statement that something is wrong or not satisfactory
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شكایت (şikâyet, “complaint”), from Arabic شِكَايَة (šikāya, “complaint”).
From Ottoman Turkish شمال, from Arabic شَمَال (šamāl).
From Arabic شِرْك (širk).
From Ottoman Turkish شركت (şirket), from Arabic شِرْكَة (širka).

parole.significato: bitchy, hussy, malicious, quarrelsome, minx, shrew (someone argumentative or irritable, cheeky, rude and loud)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شرت (şirret), from Arabic شِرَّة (širra, “the being شَرّ (šarr, “evil”)”).
From Ottoman Turkish شریان (“artery”), from Arabic شِرْيَان (širyān).
From Ottoman Turkish شعاع (şüa'), from Arabic شُعَاع (šuʕāʕ).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شباط (şubat), from Arabic شُبَاط (šubāṭ), from Classical Syriac ܫܒܛ.
From Ottoman Turkish شعبه, from Arabic شُعْبَة (šuʕba).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شعله (şu'le), from Arabic شُعْلَة (šuʕla).
From Arabic شَرَاب (šarāb).
From Ottoman Turkish شعور (şuûr), from Arabic شُعُور (šuʕūr), from the root ش ع ر (š ʕ r).
From Ottoman Turkish شهرت, from Arabic شُهْرَة (šuhra).
From Ottoman Turkish شوری, شورا (şura), ًfrom Arabic شُورَى (šūrā).
From Ottoman Turkish شكران (şükran), from Arabic شُكْرَان (šukrān).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شكر (şükr, vulg. şükür, “thankfulness, gratitude”), from Arabic شُكْر (šukr, “thankfulness, gratitude”).
From Ottoman Turkish شمول (şümul), from Arabic شُمُول (šumūl), verbal noun of شَمِلَ (šamila).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شبهه (şübhe), from Arabic شُبْهَة (šubha).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شبههلو (şübheli, şüpeli, “doubtful”) or شبههلی, from شبهه (şübhe, şüpe, “a doubt, suspicion, uncertainty”), from Arabic شُبْهَة (šubha, “uncertainty, doubt, obscurity”), verbal noun of شَبِهَ (šabiha, “to resemble, to be similar”).
Ultimately from Arabic شَبُّوط (šabbūṭ). Compare dialectal Armenian շրպոթ (šrpotʻ), շրպութ (šrputʻ), շապպոթ (šappotʻ) also recorded in Palu.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شق, from Arabic شِقّ (šiqq).

parole.significato: Letter of the Arabic alphabet: ش
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شین (şîn), from Arabic شِين (šīn).

parole.significato: okra, ladies' fingers, any flowering plant of the species Abelmoschus esculentus and its seed pod
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish بامیه (bamya), from either Classical Persian بامیه (bāmiya) or Arabic بَامِيَا (bāmiyā).

parole.significato: drover, herder, herdsman, a person who drives animals, especially cattle or sheep
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جلب (celeb, “drover”), either from Arabic جَلَب (jalab, “merchandise, imported goods”) with a change of meaning, or from a variant of جَلَّاب (jallāb, “importer”).

parole.significato: a large haircloth sack or pannier
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish خرار (harar), from Arabic غِرَارَة (ḡirāra) (or from a dialect, considering the change in pronunciation).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قرناق (kırnak), from Old Anatolian Turkish قِرْنَاقْ (qırnaq), from Proto-Turkic *kïrnāk. Alternatively from Arabic غُرْنُوق (ḡurnūq). Compare Gagauz kırnak, Azerbaijani qırnaq, Turkmen gyrnak. Cognate with Turkish kız (“girl”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish منقور (mankur), مانقر (mankır), مانغر (mangur, mangır), further etymology uncertain. A derivation from Middle Mongol ᠮᠡᠩᠭᠦ (menggü, “silver”) has been proposed, although this is controversial. According to Nişanyan, from Arabic مَنْقُور (manqūr), or from Middle Mongol

parole.significato: synonym of gelgit (“ebb and flow, the tide”)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish مد و جزر (medd u cezir), or alternatively جزر و مد (cezir u medd), from Arabic مَدّ (madd) + جَزْر (jazr).

parole.significato: sesame, a tropical, Asian plant of the species Sesamum indicum
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish صوسام (susam), from older سیسم (sisam), from either Arabic سِمْسِم (simsim) or Ancient Greek σήσαμον (sḗsamon), both from Aramaic שומשומא (šumššemā, “sesame”).

parole.significato: iris, any flowering plant of the genus Iris, common in the Northern Hemisphere
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سوسن (sevsen, süsen, “iris”), from either Arabic سَوْسَن (sawsan, “lily”) or Classical Persian سوسن (sôsan, sawsan, “lily”), both from Ancient Greek σοῦσον (soûson), ultimately from Egyptian z:S:n-M9 (zšn, “lotus”).
